name: R/app_performance_ui.R
content:
# User interface of the Sensor performance menu: sensitivity, selectivity, specificity, stability, speed and
# precision from tables of results of any technique (calculations in R/performance.R, server side in
# app_performance_server.R). The ISE methods keep their own tabs under Techniques > Potentiometry.

perf_table_input = function(p, what) tagList(
  fileInput(paste0(p, "_file"), paste(what, "(CSV, one row per measurement)"), accept = ".csv"),
  downloadButton(paste0(p, "_template"), "Empty template (CSV)", class = "btn-sm mb-2"))
perf_units = function(p, sig = "µA") layout_columns(textInput(paste0(p, "_sunit"), "Signal unit", sig))
perf_result = function(p, h = "400px", note = NULL) tagList(
  card(plotOutput(paste0(p, "_plot"), height = h, fill = FALSE)),
  card(card_header("Results"), tableOutput(paste0(p, "_table")), uiOutput(paste0(p, "_notes")), downloadButton(paste0(p, "_csv"), "Results (CSV)", class = "btn-sm"),
       if (!is.null(note)) tags$p(class = "small text-muted mt-3 mb-0", note)))

perf_panel_sensitivity = function() nav_panel("Sensitivity",
  layout_sidebar(
    sidebar = sidebar(width = 330,
      perf_table_input("ps", "Calibration results"),
      helpText("Columns: concentration and signal (peak current, charge, potential or any other result). Rows with",
               "concentration 0 are blanks. Two or more blanks give the noise s for the LOD, otherwise the residual SD of the line is used."),
      layout_columns(textInput("ps_cunit", "Concentration unit", "µM"), textInput("ps_sunit", "Signal unit", "µA")),
      layout_columns(numericInput("ps_from", "Linear range from", NA, min = 0), numericInput("ps_to", "to", NA, min = 0)),
      numericInput("ps_area", "Electrode area for the slope per area (cm², optional)", NA, min = 0),
      helpText("Sensitivity is the slope of the calibration line. LOD = 3.3 s/slope and LOQ = 10 s/slope",
               "(ICH Q2(R2), 2023, section 3.2.3.3).")),
    perf_result("ps")))

perf_panel_selectivity = function() nav_panel("Selectivity",
  layout_sidebar(
    sidebar = sidebar(width = 330,
      perf_table_input("pl", "Signals of the target without and with each interferent"),
      helpText("Columns: interferent, signal_analyte (the target alone) and signal_mixture (the same target",
               "concentration with the interferent added), and optionally interferent_concentration. Repeated rows of one",
               "interferent are averaged."),
      numericInput("pl_tol", "Tolerated change (%)", 5, min = 0),
      helpText("The change is 100 × (with − without) / without. Within the tolerance, the interferent does not interfere",
               "at that concentration. Add each interferent at its expected concentration to the target at the middle of its",
               "expected range: the result holds for those concentrations (Thévenot et al., Pure Appl. Chem. 1999, 71, 2333, section 5.2).",
               "The response to each species alone is on the Specificity tab.",
               "For an ISE, use Techniques > Potentiometry > Selectivity (IUPAC methods for the selectivity coefficient).")),
    perf_result("pl")))

perf_panel_specificity = function() nav_panel("Specificity",
  layout_sidebar(
    sidebar = sidebar(width = 330,
      perf_table_input("pc", "Responses to the target and to each other species alone"),
      helpText("Columns: species, signal and target (yes for the target, no for the others), all at the same concentration."),
      perf_units("pc"),
      helpText("Cross-reactivity is the signal of each species as a percentage of the target signal. The selectivity ratio is",
               "the target signal divided by the signal of the species at the same concentration (Thévenot et al., Pure Appl.",
               "Chem. 1999, 71, 2333, section 5.2, which also recommends comparing a full calibration curve of each species",
               "with that of the target).")),
    perf_result("pc", note = "Note: this tab measures cross-reactivity, the response to each other species alone. Together with the Selectivity tab (the target with each interferent added), it describes how selective the sensor is. IUPAC recommends the term selectivity, which can be graded, and discourages specificity for the same concept. A method is either specific or not, and few methods, if any, are specific (Vessman et al., Pure Appl. Chem. 2001, 73, 1381).")))

perf_panel_stability = function() nav_panel("Stability",
  layout_sidebar(
    sidebar = sidebar(width = 330,
      perf_table_input("pt", "Signal over time"),
      helpText("Columns: time and signal, for the same standard measured at intervals (days of storage, hours of",
               "operation, or cycles). Repeated rows at one time are averaged."),
      layout_columns(textInput("pt_tunit", "Time unit", "days"), textInput("pt_sunit", "Signal unit", "µA")),
      numericInput("pt_limit", "Retention limit (%)", 90, min = 0, max = 100),
      helpText("Retention is the signal as a percentage of the first one. The time below the limit is interpolated between",
               "the two measurements on either side.")),
    perf_result("pt")))

perf_panel_speed = function() nav_panel("Speed",
  layout_sidebar(
    sidebar = sidebar(width = 330,
      file_in("pq_file", "One recording with an addition (EMF16, or an export from a potentiostat)", accept = file_types),
      selectInput("pq_channel", "EMF16 channel", choices = NULL),
      numericInput("pq_tadd", "Time of the addition (s)", NA, min = 0),
      layout_columns(numericInput("pq_pre", "Baseline before it (s)", 2, min = 0), numericInput("pq_post", "Final level over the last (s)", 10, min = 0)),
      numericInput("pq_smooth", "Running median over (s)", 0.2, min = 0),
      helpText("The baseline is the median before the addition, the final level the median at the end of the recording.",
               "t90 and t95 are the times after the addition at which the smoothed signal has covered 90% and 95% of the change.",
               "Record long enough after the addition for the signal to settle.")),
    perf_result("pq")))

perf_panel_precision = function() nav_panel("Precision",
  layout_sidebar(
    sidebar = sidebar(width = 330,
      perf_table_input("pp", "Repeated results"),
      helpText("Columns: value (one result per row, for example the signal of one standard), and any of day, electrode",
               "and laboratory. A column with only one level is ignored."),
      perf_units("pp"),
      helpText("The terms of ICH Q2(R2) are as thus. Repeatability is the precision under the same conditions over a short time.",
               "Intermediate precision covers days, analysts and equipment within one laboratory. Reproducibility is the",
               "precision between laboratories. Electrode-to-electrode variation, often called reproducibility in sensor",
               "papers, is part of the intermediate precision. Each component is a variance from a mixed model (REML, lme4).",
               "Five or more levels of each grouping are usually needed. For an ISE, the check-standard analysis is under",
               "Techniques > Potentiometry > Precision.")),
    perf_result("pp")))

performance_ui = function() nav_menu("Sensor performance",
  perf_panel_sensitivity(), perf_panel_selectivity(), perf_panel_specificity(), perf_panel_stability(), perf_panel_speed(), perf_panel_precision())

R/cell_diagram.R
content:
# Cell diagram: a clean schematic of an electrochemical cell, drawn only from what the user states. The shapes are
# generic symbols (sheathed disk, reference tube with frit, coiled wire), not a picture of the user's glassware, and
# every label is the user's own text. A blank label shows the role alone ("Working electrode"), never a guessed material.
# Layouts: one compartment with three electrodes; two compartments with a separator (potentiometric, one electrode
# per chamber, or a potentiostat with WE and RE in chamber A and CE in chamber B); a rotating disk electrode.

cell_layouts = c("One compartment, three electrodes" = "single", "Two compartments with a separator" = "two",
                 "Two electrodes (patch-clamp amplifier)" = "pc",
                 "Rotating disk electrode" = "rde")
cell_we_kinds = c("Disk electrode (sheathed)" = "disk", "Plate or foil" = "plate", "Wire" = "wire")
cell_ce_kinds = c("Coiled wire" = "coil", "Rod" = "rod", "Plate or mesh" = "plate", "Wire" = "wire")
cell_re_kinds = c("Single-junction tube with frit" = "reference", "Double-junction tube (outer salt-bridge sleeve)" = "double",
                  "Pseudo-reference wire" = "pseudo")
cell_any_kinds = c(cell_re_kinds, cell_we_kinds, "Coiled wire" = "coil", "Rod" = "rod")

cd_col = list(line = "#2f3a45", metal = "#8a939c", dark = "#3d4650", glass = "#ffffff", sol_a = "#d6e6f5",
              sol_b = "#e2efe0", sep = "#c9822f", box = "#f2f4f6", frit = "#b9c0c7")

# Drawing pieces are collected in an environment and turned into data frames at the end
cd_new = function() { e = new.env(); e$poly = list(); e$path = list(); e$arrow = list(); e$text = list(); e }
cd_poly = function(e, x, y, fill, col = cd_col$line, lw = 0.45) { i = length(e$poly) + 1
  e$poly[[i]] = data.frame(x = x, y = y, fill = fill, col = col, lw = lw, id = i) }
cd_rect = function(e, x0, x1, y0, y1, ...) cd_poly(e, c(x0, x1, x1, x0), c(y0, y0, y1, y1), ...)
cd_path = function(e, x, y, col = cd_col$line, lw = 0.5, arrow = FALSE) { k = if (arrow) "arrow" else "path"; i = length(e[[k]]) + 1
  e[[k]][[i]] = data.frame(x = x, y = y, col = col, lw = lw, id = i) }
cd_text = function(e, x, y, label, size = 3.6, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, face = "plain")
  e$text[[length(e$text) + 1]] = data.frame(x = x, y = y, label = label, size = size, hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust, face = face)
cd_arc = function(cx, cy, r, a0, a1, n = 16) { a = seq(a0, a1, length.out = n); list(x = cx + r * cos(a), y = cy + r * sin(a)) }
cd_circle = function(e, cx, cy, r, ...) { a = cd_arc(cx, cy, r, 0, 2 * pi, 40); cd_poly(e, a$x, a$y, ...) }

# Open vessel with rounded bottom corners, and the solution inside it up to the level
cd_vessel_outline = function(x0, x1, top, r = 0.7) {
  a1 = cd_arc(x0 + r, r, r, pi, 1.5 * pi); a2 = cd_arc(x1 - r, r, r, 1.5 * pi, 2 * pi)
  list(x = c(x0, a1$x, a2$x, x1), y = c(top, a1$y, a2$y, top)) }
cd_solution = function(e, x0, x1, level, fill, round_left = TRUE, round_right = TRUE, r = 0.7) {
  left = if (round_left) cd_arc(x0 + r, r, r, pi, 1.5 * pi) else list(x = x0, y = 0)
  right = if (round_right) cd_arc(x1 - r, r, r, 1.5 * pi, 2 * pi) else list(x = x1, y = 0)
  cd_poly(e, c(x0, left$x, right$x, x1), c(level, left$y, right$y, level), fill = fill, col = NA, lw = 0) }

# One electrode at x = cx, from its tip up to top; the shape is the symbol chosen by the user
cd_electrode = function(e, kind, cx, tip, top) {
  if (cd_is3d(e) && kind %in% c("disk", "rde", "reference", "double", "rod", "plate")) return(cd_electrode3d(e, kind, cx, tip, top))
  switch(kind,
    disk = { cd_rect(e, cx - 0.35, cx + 0.35, tip, top, fill = cd_col$glass); cd_rect(e, cx - 0.24, cx + 0.24, tip, tip + 0.16, fill = cd_col$dark) },
    plate = { cd_path(e, c(cx, cx), c(tip + 2.2, top), lw = 0.6); cd_rect(e, cx - 0.5, cx + 0.5, tip, tip + 2.2, fill = cd_col$metal) },
    wire = cd_path(e, c(cx, cx), c(tip, top), col = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.9),
    rod = cd_rect(e, cx - 0.2, cx + 0.2, tip, top, fill = cd_col$dark),
    coil = { cd_path(e, c(cx, cx), c(tip + 2, top), col = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.7)
             t = seq(0, 6 * 2 * pi, length.out = 240)
             cd_path(e, cx + 0.38 * sin(t), tip + 2 - 2 * t / max(t), col = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.7) },
    reference = { cd_rect(e, cx - 0.4, cx + 0.4, tip, top, fill = "#f7fafc")
                  cd_rect(e, cx - 0.4, cx + 0.4, tip, tip + 0.35, fill = cd_col$frit)
                  cd_path(e, c(cx, cx), c(tip + 1.6, top), col = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.5)
                  cd_rect(e, cx - 0.09, cx + 0.09, tip + 0.8, tip + 1.6, fill = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.3) },
    double = { cd_rect(e, cx - 0.55, cx + 0.55, tip, tip + 4.2, fill = "#eef3f8")
               cd_rect(e, cx - 0.55, cx + 0.55, tip, tip + 0.35, fill = cd_col$frit)
               cd_rect(e, cx - 0.3, cx + 0.3, tip + 0.9, top, fill = "#f7fafc")
               cd_rect(e, cx - 0.3, cx + 0.3, tip + 0.9, tip + 1.2, fill = cd_col$frit)
               cd_path(e, c(cx, cx), c(tip + 2.4, top), col = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.5)
               cd_rect(e, cx - 0.08, cx + 0.08, tip + 1.6, tip + 2.4, fill = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.3) },
    pseudo = cd_path(e, c(cx, cx), c(tip, top), col = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.9),
    ume = { cd_rect(e, cx - 0.3, cx + 0.3, tip + 1.4, top, fill = cd_col$glass)
            cd_poly(e, c(cx - 0.3, cx - 0.1, cx + 0.1, cx + 0.3), c(tip + 1.4, tip, tip, tip + 1.4), fill = cd_col$glass, lw = 0.45)
            cd_path(e, c(cx, cx), c(tip + 0.06, top), col = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.4)
            cd_rect(e, cx - 0.05, cx + 0.05, tip, tip + 0.06, fill = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.2) },
    rde = { cd_rect(e, cx - 0.45, cx + 0.45, tip, top, fill = cd_col$glass); cd_rect(e, cx - 0.3, cx + 0.3, tip, tip + 0.16, fill = cd_col$dark)
            a = cd_arc(cx, top - 1.2, 1, 0.75 * pi, 2.25 * pi, 30); cd_path(e, a$x, top - 1.2 + (a$y - (top - 1.2)) * 0.3, lw = 0.5, arrow = TRUE) },
    stop("unknown electrode symbol: ", kind))
}

# 3D style (optional): restrained perspective. Elliptical rims, caps and liquid surface, a light highlight and a
# faint shade on each cylinder, and a box in oblique view for the two-compartment cell. No glossy gradients; the
# labels and their positions are the same as in the flat style.
cd_ry = 0.6; cd_dx = 1.2; cd_dy = 0.75
cd_ell = function(xc, yc, rx, ry, a0, a1, n = 48) { a = seq(a0, a1, length.out = n); list(x = xc + rx * cos(a), y = yc + ry * sin(a)) }
cd_is3d = function(e) identical(e$style, "3d")

# Beaker as a cylinder: curved base, rim ellipse (back half lighter), and an elliptical liquid surface
cd_vessel3d = function(e, x0, x1, top) {
  xc = (x0 + x1) / 2; rx = (x1 - x0) / 2; f = cd_ell(xc, cd_ry, rx, cd_ry, pi, 2 * pi)
  cd_path(e, c(x0, f$x, x1), c(top, f$y, top), lw = 0.9)
  b = cd_ell(xc, top, rx, cd_ry, 0, pi); cd_path(e, b$x, b$y, col = "#8a96a3", lw = 0.6)
  r = cd_ell(xc, top, rx, cd_ry, pi, 2 * pi); cd_path(e, r$x, r$y, lw = 0.9)
}
cd_solution3d = function(e, x0, x1, level, fill, surface) {
  xc = (x0 + x1) / 2; rx = (x1 - x0) / 2; f = cd_ell(xc, cd_ry, rx, cd_ry, pi, 2 * pi)
  cd_poly(e, c(x0, f$x, x1), c(level, f$y, level), fill = fill, col = NA, lw = 0)
  s = cd_ell(xc, level, rx, cd_ry, 0, 2 * pi); cd_poly(e, s$x, s$y, fill = surface, col = "#7fa7cf", lw = 0.4)
}

# Two-compartment cell as a box: liquid tops and the right face of chamber B (drawn before the electrodes), then
# the box edges and the separator set in the dividing wall (drawn after)
cd_box3d_liquid = function(e, x0, xm, x1, level) {
  cd_poly(e, c(x0, xm, xm + cd_dx, x0 + cd_dx), c(level, level, level + cd_dy, level + cd_dy), fill = "#e6f0f9", col = "#7fa7cf", lw = 0.4)
  cd_poly(e, c(xm, x1, x1 + cd_dx, xm + cd_dx), c(level, level, level + cd_dy, level + cd_dy), fill = "#edf5ec", col = "#8fbf8a", lw = 0.4)
  cd_poly(e, c(x1, x1 + cd_dx, x1 + cd_dx, x1), c(0, cd_dy, level + cd_dy, level), fill = "#d3e6d0", col = NA, lw = 0)
}
cd_box3d_frame = function(e, x0, xm, x1, top, o1, o2) {
  cd_path(e, c(x1, x1 + cd_dx, x1 + cd_dx, x1), c(0, cd_dy, top + cd_dy, top), lw = 0.9)
  cd_path(e, c(x0, x0 + cd_dx, x1 + cd_dx), c(top, top + cd_dy, top + cd_dy), col = "#8a96a3", lw = 0.6)
  cd_path(e, c(xm, xm + cd_dx), c(top, top + cd_dy), col = "#8a96a3", lw = 0.6)
  cd_poly(e, c(xm, xm + cd_dx, xm + cd_dx, xm), c(o1, o1 + cd_dy, o2 + cd_dy, o2), fill = "#c9822fb3", col = cd_col$sep, lw = 0.5)
}

# Cylinder look for a straight electrode body from y0 to y1: highlight, shade, rounded bottom edge and a top cap
cd_cyl = function(e, cx, hw, y0, y1, body, bottom = body) {
  ry = hw * 0.32
  cd_rect(e, cx - hw * 0.62, cx - hw * 0.28, y0, y1, fill = "#FFFFFFA6", col = NA, lw = 0)
  cd_rect(e, cx + hw * 0.58, cx + hw - 0.03, y0, y1, fill = "#0000001A", col = NA, lw = 0)
  b = cd_ell(cx, y0, hw, ry, pi, 2 * pi)
  cd_poly(e, c(cx - hw, b$x, cx + hw), c(y0 + 0.04, b$y, y0 + 0.04), fill = bottom, col = NA, lw = 0)
  cd_path(e, c(cx - hw, b$x, cx + hw), c(y0, b$y, y0), lw = 0.45)
  t = cd_ell(cx, y1, hw, ry, 0, 2 * pi); cd_poly(e, t$x, t$y, fill = body, lw = 0.45)
}
cd_electrode3d = function(e, kind, cx, tip, top) {
  switch(kind,
    disk = { cd_rect(e, cx - 0.35, cx + 0.35, tip, top, fill = cd_col$glass); cd_cyl(e, cx, 0.35, tip, top, cd_col$glass)
             d = cd_ell(cx, tip - 0.02, 0.26, 0.085, 0, 2 * pi); cd_poly(e, d$x, d$y, fill = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.3) },
    rde = { cd_rect(e, cx - 0.45, cx + 0.45, tip, top, fill = cd_col$glass); cd_cyl(e, cx, 0.45, tip, top, cd_col$glass)
            d = cd_ell(cx, tip - 0.02, 0.32, 0.1, 0, 2 * pi); cd_poly(e, d$x, d$y, fill = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.3)
            a = cd_arc(cx, top - 1.2, 1, 0.75 * pi, 2.25 * pi, 30); cd_path(e, a$x, top - 1.2 + (a$y - (top - 1.2)) * 0.3, lw = 0.5, arrow = TRUE) },
    reference = { cd_rect(e, cx - 0.4, cx + 0.4, tip, top, fill = "#f7fafc"); cd_rect(e, cx - 0.4, cx + 0.4, tip, tip + 0.35, fill = cd_col$frit)
                  cd_path(e, c(cx, cx), c(tip + 1.6, top), col = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.5)
                  cd_rect(e, cx - 0.09, cx + 0.09, tip + 0.8, tip + 1.6, fill = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.3)
                  cd_cyl(e, cx, 0.4, tip, top, "#f7fafc", cd_col$frit) },
    double = { cd_rect(e, cx - 0.55, cx + 0.55, tip, tip + 4.2, fill = "#eef3f8"); cd_rect(e, cx - 0.55, cx + 0.55, tip, tip + 0.35, fill = cd_col$frit)
               cd_cyl(e, cx, 0.55, tip, tip + 4.2, "#eef3f8", cd_col$frit)
               cd_rect(e, cx - 0.3, cx + 0.3, tip + 0.9, top, fill = "#f7fafc"); cd_rect(e, cx - 0.3, cx + 0.3, tip + 0.9, tip + 1.2, fill = cd_col$frit)
               cd_path(e, c(cx, cx), c(tip + 2.4, top), col = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.5)
               cd_rect(e, cx - 0.08, cx + 0.08, tip + 1.6, tip + 2.4, fill = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.3)
               cd_cyl(e, cx, 0.3, tip + 0.9, top, "#f7fafc", cd_col$frit) },
    rod = { cd_rect(e, cx - 0.2, cx + 0.2, tip, top, fill = cd_col$dark); cd_cyl(e, cx, 0.2, tip, top, cd_col$dark) },
    plate = { cd_path(e, c(cx, cx), c(tip + 2.2, top), lw = 0.6); cd_rect(e, cx - 0.5, cx + 0.5, tip, tip + 2.2, fill = cd_col$metal)
              cd_poly(e, c(cx + 0.5, cx + 0.64, cx + 0.64, cx + 0.5), c(tip, tip + 0.1, tip + 2.3, tip + 2.2), fill = "#6f7881", lw = 0.4)
              cd_poly(e, c(cx - 0.5, cx + 0.5, cx + 0.64, cx - 0.36), c(tip + 2.2, tip + 2.2, tip + 2.3, tip + 2.3), fill = "#aab2b9", lw = 0.4) },
    cd_electrode(e, kind, cx, tip, top))
}
cd_instrument3d = function(e, x0, x1, top) {
  t = top + 4.9; b = top + 2.6; dx = 0.7; dy = 0.45
  cd_poly(e, c(x0, x1, x1 + dx, x0 + dx), c(t, t, t + dy, t + dy), fill = "#e3e7eb", lw = 0.45)
  cd_poly(e, c(x1, x1 + dx, x1 + dx, x1), c(b, b + dy, t + dy, t), fill = "#d5dadf", lw = 0.45)
}

# Instrument box across the top, with one straight lead per electrode and terminal names where they apply
cd_instrument = function(e, label, xs, terminals, x0, x1, top) {
  cd_rect(e, x0, x1, top + 2.6, top + 4.9, fill = cd_col$box)
  if (cd_is3d(e)) cd_instrument3d(e, x0, x1, top)
  cd_text(e, (x0 + x1) / 2, top + 4.25, label, size = 4.8, face = "bold")
  for (i in seq_along(xs)) {
    cd_path(e, c(xs[i], xs[i]), c(top, top + 2.6), lw = 0.45)
    cd_circle(e, xs[i], top + 2.6, 0.13, fill = cd_col$line, lw = 0.3)
    if (nzchar(terminals[i])) cd_text(e, xs[i], top + 3.2, terminals[i], size = 3.9, face = "bold")
  }
}

# Digits that follow an element symbol or a closing bracket become subscripts: H2SO4 to H₂SO₄, N2 to N₂, Mg(ClO4)2 to
# Mg(ClO₄)₂. Used only for solutions, electrolyte and gas (not electrode or instrument names such as CHI760E), and only
# when the user leaves the option on. Concentrations such as "0.5 M" are untouched: their digits do not follow a letter.
cd_subscripts = function(x) {
  sub_digit = function(d) chartr("0123456789", "₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉", d)
  m = gregexpr("(?<=[A-Za-z)\\]])[0-9]+", x, perl = TRUE)
  regmatches(x, m) = lapply(regmatches(x, m), sub_digit)
  x
}

# One entry as text for the report: the role, then the user's text if any
cd_entry = function(role, value) { v = trimws(value %||% ""); if (nzchar(v)) paste0(role, ": ", v) else role }

# Half-width of an electrode symbol at height y, so a leader starts at the edge of the part and not inside it
cd_halfwidth = function(kind, tip, y) switch(kind, disk = 0.35, ume = if (y < tip + 1.4) 0.2 else 0.3, rde = 0.45, reference = 0.4, double = if (y < tip + 4.2) 0.55 else 0.3,
  plate = if (y < tip + 2.2) 0.5 else 0, rod = 0.2, coil = if (y < tip + 2) 0.38 else 0, 0)

# Labels beside the drawing, each joined to its part by a thin leader. The anchor (ax, ay) is on the part; the leader
# runs level from the anchor to just past the vessel wall, so ay is a height where nothing else is in the way, then
# bends to its label. Labels keep the top-to-bottom order of their anchors, so leaders on one side never cross.
cd_callouts = function(e, items, side, wall, floor = -1.2) {
  if (!length(items)) return(0)
  items = items[order(-vapply(items, `[[`, 0, "ay"))]
  # role only in "full" labels; in "short" labels the role is NULL and only the description is shown (all text bold)
  lines = lapply(items, function(it) c(it$role, unlist(lapply(it$values[nzchar(trimws(it$values))], strwrap, 26))))
  h = (lengths(lines) - 1) * 0.95; ly = vapply(items, `[[`, 0, "ay")
  for (i in seq_along(items)[-1]) ly[i] = min(ly[i], ly[i - 1] - h[i - 1] / 2 - h[i] / 2 - 1.25)
  low = min(ly - h / 2); if (low < floor) ly = ly + (floor - low)
  s = if (side == "left") -1 else 1; xa = wall + s * 0.6; xb = wall + s * 1.4; xt = wall + s * 1.65
  for (i in seq_along(items)) { it = items[[i]]
    cd_path(e, c(it$ax, xa, xb), c(it$ay, it$ay, ly[i]), col = "#6b7682", lw = 0.35)
    cd_circle(e, it$ax, it$ay, 0.09, fill = "#6b7682", col = NA, lw = 0)
    y1 = ly[i] + h[i] / 2
    for (j in seq_along(lines[[i]])) cd_text(e, xt, y1 - (j - 1) * 0.95, lines[[i]][j], size = 4.2,
                                             hjust = if (side == "left") 1 else 0, face = "bold")
  }
  max(nchar(unlist(lines)))
}
cd_item = function(ax, ay, role, ...) list(ax = ax, ay = ay, role = role, values = c(...))

# spec: a list with layout and the user's entries (see the app's Cell diagram tab). Returns the plot and the entries.
cell_diagram = function(spec) {
  g = function(k, d = "") { v = spec[[k]]; if (is.null(v) || (length(v) == 1 && is.na(v))) d else v }
  f = function(k) if (isTRUE(spec$subscripts)) cd_subscripts(g(k)) else g(k)
  e = cd_new(); e$style = g("style", "flat"); is3d = cd_is3d(e); L = list(); R = list(); entries = character(0)
  # each label is added to one side and to the report entries; an optional part (analyte, gas, rotation) only when entered or ticked
  # labels: "short" shows only the user's description (RE, WE and CE at the instrument already name the electrodes),
  # "full" adds the role, "none" draws no outside labels. The report entries are the same in every case.
  labels = g("labels", "short")
  lab = function(side, ax, ay, role, value = "", extra = NULL) {
    desc = c(value, extra); has_desc = any(nzchar(trimws(desc)))
    if (labels == "full" || (labels == "short" && has_desc)) {
      it = cd_item(ax, ay, if (labels == "full") role else NULL, value, extra)
      if (side == "left") L[[length(L) + 1]] <<- it else R[[length(R) + 1]] <<- it
    }
    entries <<- c(entries, cd_entry(role, value), extra)
  }
  layout = g("layout", "single"); top = 12.5
  analyte = f("analyte"); has_analyte = nzchar(trimws(analyte))
  # electrolyte and analyte are written inside the liquid (no leaders), in a band at the bottom of each compartment that
  # the electrodes do not reach; chamber names the compartment: "single", "A" or "B"
  inside = list()
  content = function(chamber, role, value) {
    entries <<- c(entries, cd_entry(role, value))
    txt = if (labels == "full") cd_entry(role, value) else if (labels == "short") trimws(value) else ""
    if (nzchar(txt)) inside[[length(inside) + 1]] <<- list(chamber = chamber, text = txt, analyte = startsWith(role, "Analyte"))
  }
  if (layout %in% c("single", "rde")) {
    x0 = 0; x1 = 10; level = 8; xs = c(RE = 2.3, WE = 4.6, CE = 8.2)
    we_kind = if (layout == "rde") "rde" else g("we_kind", "disk"); re_kind = g("re_kind", "reference"); ce_kind = g("ce_kind", "coil")
    we_tip = if (layout == "rde") 4 else 4.2; re_tip = 4.9; ce_tip = 4
    if (is3d) cd_solution3d(e, x0, x1, level, cd_col$sol_a, "#e6f0f9") else cd_solution(e, x0, x1, level, cd_col$sol_a)
    stir = isTRUE(spec$stir) && layout == "single"; purge = isTRUE(spec$purge)
    # stir bar as a white capsule: most stir bars are PTFE-coated
    if (stir) { r = 0.19; a1 = cd_arc(4.3, 0.45, r, 0.5 * pi, 1.5 * pi); a2 = cd_arc(5.7, 0.45, r, -0.5 * pi, 0.5 * pi)
      cd_poly(e, c(a1$x, a2$x), c(a1$y, a2$y), fill = "#ffffff", lw = 0.5) }
    cd_electrode(e, we_kind, xs[["WE"]], we_tip, top); cd_electrode(e, re_kind, xs[["RE"]], re_tip, top); cd_electrode(e, ce_kind, xs[["CE"]], ce_tip, top)
    # the gas tube sits between WE and CE, so the CE leader runs clear to the right wall
    if (purge) { cd_path(e, c(6.4, 6.4), c(3.6, top), col = cd_col$dark, lw = 0.6)
      for (b in seq(4.2, 7.4, by = 0.8)) cd_circle(e, 6.4 + 0.18 * sin(b * 3), b, 0.14, fill = "#ffffff", lw = 0.35) }
    if (is3d) cd_vessel3d(e, x0, x1, 10) else { o = cd_vessel_outline(x0, x1, 10); cd_path(e, o$x, o$y, lw = 0.9)
      cd_path(e, c(x0 + 0.05, x1 - 0.05), c(level, level), col = "#7fa7cf", lw = 0.4) }
    cd_instrument(e, if (nzchar(trimws(g("instrument")))) g("instrument") else "Potentiostat", xs, c("RE", "WE", "CE"), x0 - 0.5, x1 + 0.5, top)
    lab("left", xs[["RE"]] - cd_halfwidth(re_kind, re_tip, 9), 9, "Reference electrode", g("re"))
    # the WE leader runs under the tip of the reference electrode (between 4.2 and 4.9)
    rot = trimws(g("rotation"))
    lab("left", xs[["WE"]] - cd_halfwidth(we_kind, we_tip, 4.55), 4.55, if (layout == "rde") "Rotating disk electrode" else "Working electrode",
        g("we"), if (layout == "rde" && nzchar(rot)) paste("Rotation:", rot))
    lab("right", xs[["CE"]] + cd_halfwidth(ce_kind, ce_tip, 9), 9, "Counter electrode", g("ce"))
    # the gas leader runs from the end of the tube, under the counter electrode
    if (purge) lab("right", 6.4, 3.65, "Gas purge", f("gas"))
    # the stir bar sits at the centre of the bottom; its leader runs under the gas tube and the counter electrode
    if (stir) lab("right", 5.9, 0.45, "Stir bar")
    content("single", "Electrolyte", f("electrolyte")); if (has_analyte) content("single", "Analyte", analyte)
    band = list(single = c((x0 + x1) / 2, if (stir) 1.25 else 0.75, if (purge) 3.3 else min(we_tip, ce_tip) - 0.45))
  } else if (layout == "pc") {
    # two electrodes on a patch-clamp amplifier, no counter electrode: the ultramicroelectrode on the headstage input and
    # the Ag/AgCl electrode on ground (Axon convention: potential at the headstage input with respect to ground)
    x0 = 0; x1 = 10; level = 8; xs = c(UME = 3.2, AG = 7.0)
    re_kind = g("re_kind", "reference"); ume_tip = 4.2; re_tip = 4.9
    if (is3d) cd_solution3d(e, x0, x1, level, cd_col$sol_a, "#e6f0f9") else cd_solution(e, x0, x1, level, cd_col$sol_a)
    # particles as small dots on a fixed, evenly scattered pattern (the R2 low-discrepancy sequence, no random numbers),
    # clear of the electrodes and the text
    if (isTRUE(spec$particles)) for (i in 1:60) { px = 0.6 + 8.8 * ((0.5 + i * 0.7548776662) %% 1); py = 4.0 + 3.6 * ((0.5 + i * 0.5698402910) %% 1)
      if (abs(px - xs[["UME"]]) > 0.6 && abs(px - xs[["AG"]]) > 0.8) cd_circle(e, px, py, 0.07, fill = cd_col$dark, col = NA, lw = 0) }
    cd_electrode(e, "ume", xs[["UME"]], ume_tip, top); cd_electrode(e, re_kind, xs[["AG"]], re_tip, top)
    if (is3d) cd_vessel3d(e, x0, x1, 10) else { o = cd_vessel_outline(x0, x1, 10); cd_path(e, o$x, o$y, lw = 0.9)
      cd_path(e, c(x0 + 0.05, x1 - 0.05), c(level, level), col = "#7fa7cf", lw = 0.4) }
    cd_instrument(e, if (nzchar(trimws(g("instrument")))) g("instrument") else "Patch-clamp amplifier", xs, c("Headstage", "Ground"), x0 - 0.5, x1 + 0.5, top)
    lab("left", xs[["UME"]] - cd_halfwidth("ume", ume_tip, 9), 9, "Working electrode", g("we"))
    lab("right", xs[["AG"]] + cd_halfwidth(re_kind, re_tip, 9), 9, "Reference and counter electrode", g("re"))
    content("single", "Electrolyte", f("electrolyte")); if (has_analyte) content("single", "Analyte", analyte)
    band = list(single = c((x0 + x1) / 2, 0.75, min(ume_tip, re_tip) - 0.45))
  } else if (layout == "two") {
    x0 = 0; xm = 10; x1 = 20; level = 8.5; o1 = 3; o2 = 6
    rr = if (is3d) 0.01 else 0.7
    cd_solution(e, x0, xm, level, cd_col$sol_a, round_right = FALSE, r = rr); cd_solution(e, xm, x1, level, cd_col$sol_b, round_left = FALSE, r = rr)
    if (is3d) cd_box3d_liquid(e, x0, xm, x1, level)
    potentiometric = g("mode", "potentiometric") == "potentiometric"
    if (potentiometric) {
      ka = g("a_kind", "reference"); kb = g("b_kind", "reference")
      xs = c(5, 15); cd_electrode(e, ka, 5, 6.4, top); cd_electrode(e, kb, 15, 6.4, top); terms = c("", ""); instr_default = "Potentiometer"
    } else {
      we_kind = g("we_kind", "disk"); re_kind = g("re_kind", "reference"); ce_kind = g("ce_kind", "coil")
      xs = c(3.5, 6.5, 15); cd_electrode(e, re_kind, 3.5, 6.9, top); cd_electrode(e, we_kind, 6.5, 6.2, top); cd_electrode(e, ce_kind, 15, 5.8, top)
      terms = c("RE", "WE", "CE"); instr_default = "Potentiostat"
    }
    o = cd_vessel_outline(x0, x1, 10, r = rr); cd_path(e, o$x, o$y, lw = 0.9)
    if (is3d) cd_box3d_frame(e, x0, xm, x1, 10, o1, o2)
    cd_path(e, c(xm, xm), c(0, o1), lw = 0.9); cd_path(e, c(xm, xm), c(o2, 10), lw = 0.9)
    cd_path(e, c(xm, xm), c(o1, o2), col = cd_col$sep, lw = 3)
    cd_path(e, c(x0 + 0.05, xm - 0.05), c(level, level), col = "#7fa7cf", lw = 0.4)
    cd_path(e, c(xm + 0.05, x1 - 0.05), c(level, level), col = "#8fbf8a", lw = 0.4)
    cd_instrument(e, if (nzchar(trimws(g("instrument")))) g("instrument") else instr_default, xs, terms, x0 - 0.5, x1 + 0.5, top)
    if (potentiometric) {
      lab("left", 5 - cd_halfwidth(ka, 6.4, 9.2), 9.2, "Electrode in chamber A", g("a"))
      lab("right", 15 + cd_halfwidth(kb, 6.4, 9.2), 9.2, "Electrode in chamber B", g("b"))
    } else {
      lab("left", 3.5 - cd_halfwidth(re_kind, 6.9, 9.2), 9.2, "Reference electrode", g("re"))
      # the WE leader runs under the tip of the reference electrode
      lab("left", 6.5 - cd_halfwidth(we_kind, 6.2, 6.55), 6.55, "Working electrode", g("we"))
      lab("right", 15 + cd_halfwidth(ce_kind, 5.8, 9.2), 9.2, "Counter electrode", g("ce"))
    }
    # the separator leader runs under every electrode tip in chamber A and above the text band
    lab("left", xm, 4.5, "Separator", g("separator"))
    content("A", "Chamber A", f("sol_a")); content("B", "Chamber B", f("sol_b"))
    in_b = g("analyte_ch", "B") == "B"
    if (has_analyte) content(if (in_b) "B" else "A", paste("Analyte, chamber", if (in_b) "B" else "A"), analyte)
    band = list(A = c((x0 + xm) / 2, 0.75, 4.05), B = c((xm + x1) / 2, 0.75, 4.05))
  } else stop("unknown layout: ", layout)

  # text inside the liquid: bold, centred in the compartment, lines stacked upward from the bottom of the band and
  # wrapped to the compartment width
  for (ch in names(band)) {
    its = Filter(function(it) it$chamber == ch, inside)
    txt = vapply(its, `[[`, "", "text")
    if (!length(txt)) next
    # short labels: a centred "+" on its own line between the electrolyte and the analyte, as methods sections write
    # "0.1 M KOH + 50 mM ethanol"; each entry stays whole and wraps cleanly
    is_an = vapply(its, `[[`, TRUE, "analyte")
    plus = labels == "short" && any(is_an) && any(!is_an)
    # largest size at which the lines fit between the bottom of the band and its top limit; smaller text wraps wider
    for (sz in c(5, 4.4, 3.8, 3.3)) {
      wr = round(22 * 5 / sz); sp = 0.9 * sz / 5
      w = if (plus) c(unlist(lapply(txt[!is_an], strwrap, wr)), "+", unlist(lapply(txt[is_an], strwrap, wr))) else unlist(lapply(txt, strwrap, wr))
      if (band[[ch]][2] + (length(w) - 1) * sp + 0.25 <= band[[ch]][3]) break
    }
    for (j in seq_along(w)) cd_text(e, band[[ch]][1], band[[ch]][2] + (length(w) - j) * sp, w[j], size = sz, face = "bold")
  }

  wl = cd_callouts(e, L, "left", x0); wr = cd_callouts(e, R, "right", x1 + if (is3d && layout == "two") cd_dx else 0)
  if (is3d && layout == "two") x1 = x1 + cd_dx
  # about 0.33 plot units per bold character at this text size, so the labels fit inside the plot
  xl = x0 - 1.65 - wl * 0.33 - 0.3; xr = x1 + 1.65 + wr * 0.33 + 0.3
  title = trimws(g("title")); if (nzchar(title)) cd_text(e, min(xl, x0 - 0.5), top + 6.2, title, size = 5.4, hjust = 0, face = "bold")
  ys = c(unlist(lapply(e$text, `[[`, "y")), 0)

  P = do.call(rbind, e$poly); Ln = do.call(rbind, e$path); A = if (length(e$arrow)) do.call(rbind, e$arrow); Tx = do.call(rbind, e$text)
  p = ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::geom_polygon(data = P, ggplot2::aes(x, y, group = id, fill = fill, colour = col, linewidth = lw)) +
    ggplot2::geom_path(data = Ln, ggplot2::aes(x, y, group = id, colour = col, linewidth = lw), lineend = "round") +
    (if (!is.null(A)) ggplot2::geom_path(data = A, ggplot2::aes(x, y, group = id, colour = col, linewidth = lw),
                                         arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(2.2, "mm"), type = "closed"))) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(data = Tx, ggplot2::aes(x, y, label = label, size = size, hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust, fontface = face), colour = cd_col$line) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_identity() + ggplot2::scale_colour_identity() + ggplot2::scale_linewidth_identity() + ggplot2::scale_size_identity() +
    ggplot2::coord_fixed(clip = "off", xlim = c(min(xl, x0 - 1), xr), ylim = c(min(-0.8, min(ys) - 0.6), top + 6.9)) +
    ggplot2::theme_void() + ggplot2::theme(plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))
  list(plot = p, key = data.frame(Part = entries, check.names = FALSE))
}

content:
# Electrochemically active surface area of gold from the oxide reduction peak
# in a CV recorded in H2SO4. ECSA = Q / q_ref, with Q the charge under the
# reduction peak above a linear baseline and q_ref = 390 uC/cm2 for a monolayer
# of gold oxide (Trasatti and Petrii 1991, Pure Appl. Chem. 63, 711-734).

# Sweeps where the potential falls are the cathodic ones; the analysis uses the last
# stable cycle, so by default the last cathodic sweep in the file.
cathodic_segments = function(data) {
  s = tapply(data$E_V, data$segment, function(e) mean(diff(e)))
  as.integer(names(s)[s < 0])
}

# Baseline limits: walk out from the peak on each side until the smoothed current
# changes by less than flat_frac of the peak height per 10 mV, i.e. until the
# current has returned to a flat region.
suggest_limits = function(E, I, peak_i, flat_frac = 0.001, smooth_n = 11) {
  Is = stats::filter(I, rep(1 / smooth_n, smooth_n), sides = 2)
  Is[is.na(Is)] = I[is.na(Is)]
  step = stats::median(abs(diff(E)))
  k = max(1, round(0.01 / step))
  tol = flat_frac * abs(I[peak_i])
  walk = function(dir) {
    j = peak_i
    while (j + dir * k >= 1 && j + dir * k <= length(E)) {
      if (abs(Is[j + dir * k] - Is[j]) < tol && abs(E[j] - E[peak_i]) > 0.05) break
      j = j + dir * k
    }
    j
  }
  sort(c(E[walk(-1)], E[walk(1)]))
}

ecsa_gold = function(x, q_ref_uC_cm2 = 390, segment = NULL, limits = NULL,
                     geometric_area_cm2 = NULL) {
  d = x$data
  v = x$params$scan_rate_V_s
  if (is.null(v) || is.na(v)) stop("Scan rate unknown for ", x$file)
  cath = cathodic_segments(d)
  if (is.null(segment)) segment = max(cath)
  s = d[d$segment == segment, ]

  # Peak search skips the first and last 15% of the sweep, where the current
  # rises towards the potential limits rather than forming the oxide peak.
  n = nrow(s)
  inner = seq(ceiling(0.15 * n), floor(0.85 * n))
  peak_i = inner[which.min(s$I_A[inner])]
  # On the cathodic sweep the oxide reduction peak is a negative current. A positive peak much larger than any negative
  # current means the sign is inverted (leads or current polarity reversed): the limits would then span the whole sweep.
  inverted = max(s$I_A[inner]) > 2 * abs(min(s$I_A[inner]))

  if (is.null(limits)) limits = suggest_limits(s$E_V, s$I_A, peak_i)
  w = s$E_V >= limits[1] & s$E_V <= limits[2]
  E = s$E_V[w]
  I = s$I_A[w]
  base = stats::approx(c(E[1], E[length(E)]), c(I[1], I[length(I)]), xout = E)$y
  net = I - base

  # Charge from the potential axis: dt = dE / v, trapezoid rule.
  Q_C = abs(sum(diff(E) * (net[-1] + net[-length(net)]) / 2)) / v
  ecsa = Q_C / (q_ref_uC_cm2 * 1e-6)

  # Stability of the oxide charge over the cathodic sweeps, same limits.
  per_cycle = sapply(cath, function(g) {
    sg = d[d$segment == g & d$E_V >= limits[1] & d$E_V <= limits[2], ]
    b = stats::approx(c(sg$E_V[1], sg$E_V[nrow(sg)]), c(sg$I_A[1], sg$I_A[nrow(sg)]), xout = sg$E_V)$y
    nt = sg$I_A - b
    abs(sum(diff(sg$E_V) * (nt[-1] + nt[-length(nt)]) / 2)) / v
  })

  res = data.frame(
    file = x$file, segment = segment, scan_rate_V_s = v,
    peak_E_V = s$E_V[peak_i], peak_I_A = s$I_A[peak_i],
    lower_limit_V = limits[1], upper_limit_V = limits[2],
    Q_uC = Q_C * 1e6, q_ref_uC_cm2 = q_ref_uC_cm2, ECSA_cm2 = ecsa,
    change_last_cycle_pct = if (length(per_cycle) > 1)
      100 * (per_cycle[length(per_cycle)] / per_cycle[length(per_cycle) - 1] - 1) else NA
  )
  if (!is.null(geometric_area_cm2)) res$roughness_factor = ecsa / geometric_area_cm2
  res$note = if (inverted) "The current sign looks inverted: the reduction peak on the cathodic sweep is positive. Check the leads or the current polarity setting. This area is not valid." else ""

  chi = x$chi_peaks
  if (!is.null(chi) && any(chi$segment == segment & chi$ip_A < 0)) {
    r = chi[chi$segment == segment & chi$ip_A < 0, ]
    r = r[which.min(r$ip_A), ]
    res$chi_Ah_uC = abs(r$Ah_C) * 1e6
  }

  list(result = res, sweep = s, window = data.frame(E_V = E, I_A = I, base_A = base),
       per_cycle = data.frame(segment = cath, Q_uC = per_cycle * 1e6))
}

# Origin 2026 default line colour increment list, decoded from
# Themes/IncrementList/Line Color List.oth in the Origin installation.
origin_line_colours = c("#515151", "#F14040", "#1A6FDF", "#37AD6B", "#B177DE", "#CC9900",
                        "#00CBCC", "#7D4E4E", "#8E8E00", "#FB6501", "#6699CC", "#6FB802")

# Origin 2026 "Candy" list (Themes/Color/Candy.oth), the largest of Origin's
# lists of distinct colours; used once the default line list runs out.
origin_candy_colours = c("#EF0000", "#336699", "#FEC211", "#3BC371", "#666699", "#999999", "#FF6666",
                         "#6699CC", "#CC6600", "#009999", "#6B67BC", "#99867A", "#CC3333", "#669999",
                         "#FF9999")

# Distinct colours for the cycles other than the one used: Origin's line list
# without its dark grey (too close to the black used cycle), then Candy, with
# duplicates and the shading colour removed.
cycle_palette = function(area_fill) {
  p = unique(toupper(c(origin_line_colours[-1], origin_candy_colours)))
  p[p != toupper(area_fill)]
}

# Full CV view with the integrated oxide reduction area shaded above its
# baseline. The cycle used for ECSA is black and every other cycle gets its own
# Origin colour, listed in the legend (inside the plot for up to 8 cycles, to the
# right beyond that). Only when there are more cycles than distinct Origin
# colours are the earlier cycles coloured along the viridis scale (also an
# Origin colour map) with a colour bar, since colours would otherwise repeat.
# area_fill defaults to gold, which is kept out of the cycle colours.
plot_ecsa_cv = function(fit, x, title = NULL, reference = NULL, area_fill = "#CC9900",
                        max_inside = 8) {
  r = fit$result
  d = x$data
  w = fit$window
  ua = 1e6

  # A cycle is an anodic sweep followed by its cathodic sweep
  d$cycle = ceiling(d$segment / 2)
  used = ceiling(r$segment / 2)
  n_cyc = max(d$cycle)
  pal = cycle_palette(area_fill)
  listed = n_cyc - 1 <= length(pal)
  inside = n_cyc <= max_inside
  earlier = d[d$cycle != used, ]
  last = d[d$cycle == used, ]
  used_lab = sprintf("Cycle %d (used for ECSA)", used)

  # Direction arrows on the cycle used, away from the peaks
  an = d[d$segment == r$segment - 1, ]
  ca = d[d$segment == r$segment, ]
  arrow_at = function(s, e0, e1) {
    i0 = which.min(abs(s$E_V - e0)); i1 = which.min(abs(s$E_V - e1))
    data.frame(x = s$E_V[i0], y = s$I_A[i0] * ua, xend = s$E_V[i1], yend = s$I_A[i1] * ua)
  }
  arrows = rbind(arrow_at(an, 0.25, 0.40), arrow_at(ca, 0.45, 0.30))

  ox_form = an[an$E_V > 1.0 & an$E_V < 1.45, ]
  ox_i = which.max(ox_form$I_A)

  lab = sprintf("Q = %.2f µC\nECSA = %.4f cm²", r$Q_uC, r$ECSA_cm2)
  if (!is.null(r$roughness_factor)) lab = sprintf("%s\nRoughness factor = %.2f", lab, r$roughness_factor)

  keep = function(z) z[abs(z$E_V - r$peak_E_V) <= 0.03 & z$segment %% 2 == 0 & z$I_A <= r$peak_I_A * 0.80, ]
  tip_e = keep(earlier)
  tip_l = keep(last)

  # Earlier cycles as a listed legend or a colour bar; the inset follows the same scheme
  if (listed) {
    cyc_ids = sort(unique(earlier$cycle))
    cols = setNames(pal[seq_along(cyc_ids)], paste("Cycle", cyc_ids))
    earlier$cycle_f = factor(paste("Cycle", earlier$cycle), levels = names(cols))
    tip_e$cycle_f = factor(paste("Cycle", tip_e$cycle), levels = names(cols))
    colour_layers = list(
      ggplot2::geom_path(data = earlier, ggplot2::aes(E_V, I_A * ua, colour = cycle_f, group = cycle),
                         linewidth = 0.55),
      ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = cols, name = NULL,
                                   guide = ggplot2::guide_legend(order = 1, ncol = if (length(cols) > 14) 2 else 1)))
    inset_layers = list(
      ggplot2::geom_path(data = tip_e, ggplot2::aes(E_V, I_A * ua, colour = cycle_f, group = cycle),
                         linewidth = 0.6),
      ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = cols, guide = "none"))
  } else {
    colour_layers = list(
      ggplot2::geom_path(data = earlier, ggplot2::aes(E_V, I_A * ua, colour = cycle, group = cycle),
                         linewidth = 0.45),
      ggplot2::scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "Earlier cycles", end = 0.9,
                                      breaks = unique(round(seq(1, n_cyc - 1, length.out = 5))),
                                      guide = ggplot2::guide_colourbar(order = 1, barheight = ggplot2::unit(30, "mm"))))
    inset_layers = list(
      ggplot2::geom_path(data = tip_e, ggplot2::aes(E_V, I_A * ua, colour = cycle, group = cycle),
                         linewidth = 0.5),
      ggplot2::scale_colour_viridis_c(end = 0.9, guide = "none"))
  }

  xlab = if (is.null(reference)) "Potential (V)" else sprintf("Potential (V vs. %s)", reference)

  main = ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::geom_ribbon(data = w, ggplot2::aes(E_V, ymin = I_A * ua, ymax = base_A * ua),
                         fill = area_fill, alpha = 0.40) +
    colour_layers +
    # The used cycle gets its own legend entry through linetype, so it stays
    # black whichever colour scheme the earlier cycles use
    ggplot2::geom_path(data = last, ggplot2::aes(E_V, I_A * ua, linetype = used_lab), colour = "black",
                       linewidth = 0.75) +
    ggplot2::scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames("solid", used_lab), name = NULL,
                                   guide = ggplot2::guide_legend(order = 2)) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(floor(min(d$E_V) * 10) / 10, ceiling(max(d$E_V) * 10) / 10, by = 0.1)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(floor(min(d$I_A) * ua / 10) * 10, ceiling(max(d$I_A) * ua / 10) * 10, by = 10)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(data = w, ggplot2::aes(E_V, base_A * ua), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(data = arrows, ggplot2::aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
                          arrow = ggplot2::arrow(length = ggplot2::unit(2.2, "mm"), type = "closed"),
                          linewidth = 0.5) +
    ggplot2::annotate("segment", x = r$peak_E_V + 0.03, xend = r$peak_E_V + 0.22,
                      y = r$peak_I_A * ua * 0.40, yend = r$peak_I_A * ua * 0.40, linewidth = 0.3) +
    ggplot2::annotate("text", x = r$peak_E_V + 0.23, y = r$peak_I_A * ua * 0.40, hjust = 0, size = 3.2,
                      label = sprintf("Au oxide reduction peak\nEp = %.3f V\nShaded: area used for ECSA", r$peak_E_V)) +
    ggplot2::annotate("text", x = ox_form$E_V[ox_i], y = ox_form$I_A[ox_i] * ua + 4, size = 3.2,
                      label = "Au oxide formation") +
    # Results sit top left, in the empty space above the double-layer region,
    # so the legend can run down the left side
    ggplot2::annotate("text", x = min(d$E_V) + 0.02, y = max(d$I_A) * ua, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3.2,
                      label = lab) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = xlab, y = expression("Current ("*mu*"A)"),
                  title = if (is.null(title)) "Au electrode in 0.5 M H₂SO₄" else title,
                  subtitle = sprintf("%d cycles at %.1f V/s, ECSA from cycle %d with %g µC/cm²",
                                     n_cyc, r$scan_rate_V_s, used, r$q_ref_uC_cm2)) +
    ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 11),
                   plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
                   legend.position = if (inside) c(0.02, 0.60) else "right",
                   legend.justification = if (inside) c(0, 1) else c(0, 0.5),
                   legend.key.width = ggplot2::unit(8, "mm"),
                   legend.spacing.y = ggplot2::unit(1, "mm"),
                   legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
                   legend.background = ggplot2::element_blank())

  # The cycles overlap almost everywhere, so an inset around the reduction peak
  # tip shows how each cycle differs.
  inset = ggplot2::ggplot() +
    inset_layers +
    ggplot2::geom_path(data = tip_l, ggplot2::aes(E_V, I_A * ua), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = xlab, y = expression("Current ("*mu*"A)"), title = "Peak tip, all cycles") +
    ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 8) +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(), plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8),
                   plot.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA))

  main + patchwork::inset_element(inset, left = 0.64, bottom = 0.03, right = 0.99, top = 0.36)
}

content:
# Electrode geometry, surface-area references and the standard equations of each
# technique (voltammetry, chronoamperometry, chronocoulometry, hydrodynamic electrodes,
# impedance). Every function returns plain numbers or data frames in SI-style units
# (A, V, s, C, cm, cm2, mol/cm3 inside the equations), so the app, the report and the
# tests use the same numbers. Sources are given next to each equation and listed in
# equation_sources() for the Equations tab.

R_const = 8.314462618
if (!exists("F_const")) F_const = 96485.33212
mM_to_mol_cm3 = function(c_mM) c_mM * 1e-6

# Electrode geometry
# Disk sizes sold by the main makers, checked on the makers' pages (October 2026).
# The list only helps to fill the diameter; any other size can be typed.
electrode_sizes = data.frame(
  label = c("2 mm disk (CH Instruments CHI101 Au, CHI102 Pt, CHI103 Ag)",
            "3 mm disk (CH Instruments CHI104 glassy carbon, BASi MF-2012 glassy carbon)",
            "1.6 mm disk (BASi MF-2013 Pt, MF-2014 Au)",
            "3 mm printed carbon (CH Instruments SE101)",
            "4 mm screen-printed carbon (Metrohm DropSens 110, maker gives 0.11 cm²)",
            "5 mm disk (BioLogic glassy carbon, Pine RRDE disk)",
            "4.57 mm disk (Pine RRDE)", "5.5 mm disk (Pine RRDE)", "5.61 mm disk (Pine RRDE)",
            "25 um microdisk (CH Instruments CHI106 Au, CHI108 Pt)",
            "12.5 um microdisk (CH Instruments CHI105 Au)",
            "10 um microdisk (CH Instruments CHI107 Pt)"),
  d_mm = c(2, 3, 1.6, 3, 4, 5, 4.57, 5.5, 5.61, 0.025, 0.0125, 0.010))

# Geometric area (cm2) of common electrode shapes. Lengths in mm.
# rectangle: a flat plate or strip; faces = 1 for one exposed face (the rest masked),
#   2 for both faces; edges = TRUE adds the immersed edges of a strip of the given
#   thickness (two long edges and the bottom edge: 2 L t + W t)
# wire: a cylinder of diameter d immersed to length L, with or without its flat end
# band: a band microelectrode of length L and width W (one face)
electrode_area = function(shape = c("disk", "rectangle", "wire", "band", "hemisphere", "sphere", "area"),
                          d_mm = NA, length_mm = NA, width_mm = NA, faces = 1, edges = FALSE,
                          thickness_mm = 0, wire_end = FALSE, area_cm2 = NA) {
  shape = match.arg(shape)
  mm2 = switch(shape,
    disk = pi * (d_mm / 2)^2,
    rectangle = faces * length_mm * width_mm + if (isTRUE(edges)) 2 * length_mm * thickness_mm + width_mm * thickness_mm else 0,
    wire = pi * d_mm * length_mm + if (isTRUE(wire_end)) pi * (d_mm / 2)^2 else 0,
    band = length_mm * width_mm,
    hemisphere = 2 * pi * (d_mm / 2)^2,
    sphere = 4 * pi * (d_mm / 2)^2,
    area = area_cm2 * 100)
  mm2 / 100
}

# Surface-area reference charges
# Charge per cm2 of real surface for one monolayer, from Lukaszewski, Soszko and
# Czerwinski, Int. J. Electrochem. Sci. 11 (2016) 4442 (review, values as listed there;
# hydrogen and oxide values follow Trasatti and Petrii, Pure Appl. Chem. 63 (1991) 711).
# For PdO the review lists 424. Any other value (for example 405, which has no published source here) is typed in
# by the user, and the value used is reported.
ecsa_references = data.frame(
  key = c("pt_h", "rh_h", "ir_h", "pd_ox424", "au_ox", "pt_ox", "rh_ox", "pt_co", "cu_upd", "ag_upd", "pb_upd"),
  label = c("Pt, hydrogen desorption, 210 µC/cm²", "Rh, hydrogen desorption, 221 µC/cm²", "Ir, hydrogen desorption, 218 µC/cm²",
            "Pd, PdO reduction, 424 µC/cm²", "Au, oxide reduction, 390 µC/cm²",
            "Pt, oxide reduction, 420 µC/cm²", "Rh, oxide reduction, 442 µC/cm²", "Pt, CO stripping, 420 µC/cm²",
            "Cu underpotential deposition (stripping), 420 µC/cm²", "Ag underpotential deposition (stripping), 210 µC/cm²",
            "Pb underpotential deposition (stripping), 300 µC/cm²"),
  q_uC_cm2 = c(210, 221, 218, 424, 390, 420, 442, 420, 420, 210, 300),
  sweep = c("anodic", "anodic", "anodic", "cathodic", "cathodic", "cathodic", "cathodic", "anodic", "anodic", "anodic", "anodic"),
  source = c(rep("Lukaszewski et al. 2016 (Trasatti and Petrii 1991)", 3), "Lukaszewski et al. 2016 (Woods 1976)",
             "Lukaszewski et al. 2016 (390 ± 10)",
             rep("Lukaszewski et al. 2016", 6)))

# Double-layer capacitance from CVs in a potential range without faradaic current.
# At each scan rate the charging current is half the gap between the anodic and the
# cathodic sweep at E_at; its slope against scan rate is C_dl. ECSA = C_dl / C_s, where
# C_s (the capacitance of 1 cm2 of the same surface) must be assumed: reported values
# for metals lie mostly between 20 and 40 uF/cm2 and the error can reach 100%
# (Lukaszewski et al. 2016). Best used to compare electrodes of the same material.
cdl_from_cvs = function(xs, E_at, Cs_uF_cm2 = 40) {
  pts = do.call(rbind, lapply(xs, function(x) {
    a = last_sweep(x, "anodic", 0.02); c_ = last_sweep(x, "cathodic", 0.02)
    ia = stats::approx(a$E_V, a$I_A, E_at, ties = mean)$y; ic = stats::approx(c_$E_V, c_$I_A, E_at, ties = mean)$y
    data.frame(file = x$file, v_V_s = x$params$scan_rate_V_s, I_anodic_A = ia, I_cathodic_A = ic, I_charging_A = (ia - ic) / 2)
  }))
  pts = pts[order(pts$v_V_s), ]
  fit = if (nrow(pts) >= 2) { m = stats::lm(I_charging_A ~ v_V_s, pts)
    data.frame(n = nrow(pts), E_at_V = E_at, Cdl_uF = unname(stats::coef(m)[2]) * 1e6, intercept_A = unname(stats::coef(m)[1]),
               r2 = if (nrow(pts) > 2) summary(m)$r.squared else NA, Cs_uF_cm2 = Cs_uF_cm2,
               ECSA_cm2 = unname(stats::coef(m)[2]) * 1e6 / Cs_uF_cm2) } else NULL
  list(points = pts, fit = fit)
}

# Cyclic voltammetry: peaks and diagnostics
# Peak currents are measured from zero current (no baseline). For a second peak on a
# decaying background, or a small reverse peak, the reverse peak current read this way
# is only approximate.
sweep_peak = function(s, dir) {
  i = if (dir == "anodic") which.max(s$I_A) else which.min(s$I_A)
  ip = s$I_A[i]
  # half-peak potential: on the rising side, where the current first reaches half the peak
  before = seq_len(i)
  h = before[if (dir == "anodic") s$I_A[before] >= ip / 2 else s$I_A[before] <= ip / 2][1]
  data.frame(Ep_V = s$E_V[i], ip_A = ip, Ep_half_V = s$E_V[h])
}
cv_peaks = function(x, window = NULL, T_K = 298.15) {
  one = function(dir) {
    s = tryCatch(last_sweep(x, dir), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(s)) return(data.frame(Ep_V = NA, ip_A = NA, Ep_half_V = NA))
    if (!is.null(window)) s = s[s$E_V >= min(window) & s$E_V <= max(window), ]
    if (nrow(s) < 3) return(data.frame(Ep_V = NA, ip_A = NA, Ep_half_V = NA))
    sweep_peak(s, dir)
  }
  a = one("anodic"); c_ = one("cathodic")
  dEp = a$Ep_V - c_$Ep_V
  data.frame(file = x$file, v_V_s = x$params$scan_rate_V_s, Epa_V = a$Ep_V, ipa_A = a$ip_A, Epc_V = c_$Ep_V, ipc_A = c_$ip_A,
             dEp_mV = 1000 * dEp, E_half_V = (a$Ep_V + c_$Ep_V) / 2, ratio_ipa_ipc = abs(a$ip_A / c_$ip_A),
             Epa_minus_Ep2_mV = 1000 * abs(a$Ep_V - a$Ep_half_V), Epc_minus_Ep2_mV = 1000 * abs(c_$Ep_V - c_$Ep_half_V))
}
# Transfer coefficient from the peak shape of an irreversible wave:
# |Ep - Ep/2| = 1.857 RT / (alpha n F), 47.7/alpha mV at 25 C (Microchim. Acta 2023, 190, 251, eq. 9)
alpha_from_peak_width = function(width_mV, n = 1, T_K = 298.15) 1.857 * R_const * T_K / (n * F_const * width_mV / 1000)

# Randles-Sevcik. ip = 0.4463 n F A C (n F v D / R T)^1/2 for a reversible wave, which is
# 2.69e5 n^3/2 A D^1/2 C v^1/2 at 25 C; ip = 0.4958 n F A C (alpha n F v D / R T)^1/2 for an
# irreversible wave, 2.99e5 n alpha^1/2 A D^1/2 C v^1/2 at 25 C with n' = n = 1
# (Bard and Faulkner; Microchim. Acta 2023, 190, 251, eqs. 3 and 7).
# Units: A in cm2, D in cm2/s, C in mol/cm3, v in V/s, ip in A.
rs_coef = function(n = 1, T_K = 298.15, reversible = TRUE, alpha = 0.5)
  if (reversible) 0.4463 * n * F_const * sqrt(n * F_const / (R_const * T_K)) else 0.4958 * n * F_const * sqrt(alpha * n * F_const / (R_const * T_K))
# slope of |ip| against v^1/2 gives the area when D is known, or D when the area is known
rs_solve = function(slope_A_per_sqrtV_s, n = 1, C_mM, D_cm2_s = NA, area_cm2 = NA, T_K = 298.15, reversible = TRUE, alpha = 0.5) {
  k = rs_coef(n, T_K, reversible, alpha) * mM_to_mol_cm3(C_mM)
  data.frame(area_cm2 = if (!is.na(D_cm2_s)) slope_A_per_sqrtV_s / (k * sqrt(D_cm2_s)) else NA,
             D_cm2_s = if (!is.na(area_cm2)) (slope_A_per_sqrtV_s / (k * area_cm2))^2 else NA)
}

# Standard rate constant k0 (cm/s) from the peak separation of one CV.
# Nicholson, with the Lavagnini et al. (Electroanalysis 2004, 16, 505) fit of the working
# curve: psi = (-0.6288 + 0.0021 X) / (1 - 0.017 X), X = n dEp in mV, valid up to about
# 200 mV; k0 = psi (pi D n v F / R T)^1/2.
# Klingler and Kochi (J. Phys. Chem. 1981, 85, 1731) for n dEp above 150 mV:
# k0 = 2.18 (alpha D n v F / R T)^1/2 exp(-(alpha^2 n F / R T) dEp).
# Both as given in Microchim. Acta 2023, 190, 251 (eqs. 11 to 13, Table 1).
k0_nicholson = function(dEp_mV, v_V_s, D_cm2_s, n = 1, T_K = 298.15) {
  X = n * dEp_mV
  psi = (-0.6288 + 0.0021 * X) / (1 - 0.017 * X)
  k0 = psi * sqrt(pi * D_cm2_s * n * v_V_s * F_const / (R_const * T_K))
  ifelse(X > 61 & X <= 200, k0, NA)
}
k0_klingler_kochi = function(dEp_mV, v_V_s, D_cm2_s, alpha = 0.5, n = 1, T_K = 298.15) {
  f = n * F_const / (R_const * T_K)
  k0 = 2.18 * sqrt(alpha * D_cm2_s * n * v_V_s * F_const / (R_const * T_K)) * exp(-alpha^2 * f * dEp_mV / 1000)
  ifelse(n * dEp_mV > 150, k0, NA)
}
# Which regime the peak separation points to (Microchim. Acta 2023: reversible about
# 57 to 63 mV, quasi-reversible 63 to 200 mV, irreversible above 200 mV for n dEp)
cv_regime = function(dEp_mV, n = 1) {
  X = n * dEp_mV
  ifelse(is.na(X), NA, ifelse(X <= 63, "reversible", ifelse(X <= 200, "quasi-reversible", "irreversible")))
}

# Quasi-reversible Randles-Sevcik: ip = ip(reversible) x K(Lambda, alpha) (Matsuda and Ayabe; used for the
# electroactive area by Trachioti et al., Microchim. Acta 2023, 190, 251, eq. 4). The paper reads K off published
# graphs. Here K, the peak width Delta = (Ep/2 - Ep) F/RT and the peak separation come from a table made with a
# Butler-Volmer finite-difference simulation (one form in the bulk, equal D, first sweep, peaks from zero), checked
# against the reversible and irreversible Randles-Sevcik peaks (0.4% low, cancelled by taking K against the
# reversible run on the same grid) and Nicholson's dEp-psi values (within 2 mV). See rs_quasi_table in
# R/rs_quasi_table.R and scripts/12_rs_quasi_table.R. Lambda = k0 / sqrt(D f v) = psi sqrt(pi).
# Steps as in the paper: Lambda from n dEp, alpha from the width of the forward peak, then K(Lambda, alpha).
rs_quasi_K = function(dEp_mV, width_mV, n = 1, T_K = 298.15, tab = rs_quasi_table) {
  u = 1000 * R_const * T_K / F_const                        # RT/F in mV
  X = n * dEp_mV / u; W = n * width_mV / u
  alphas = sort(unique(tab$alpha))
  one = function(X, W) {
    if (!is.finite(X) || !is.finite(W)) return(c(NA, NA, NA, NA))
    # for each alpha in the table, the log Lambda that gives this dEp, and the width and K there
    at = t(vapply(alphas, function(a) { s = tab[tab$alpha == a, ]; s = s[order(s$dEp_RT_F), ]
      if (X < min(s$dEp_RT_F) || X > max(s$dEp_RT_F)) return(c(NA, NA, NA))
      lL = stats::approx(s$dEp_RT_F, s$log10_Lambda, X)$y
      s = s[order(s$log10_Lambda), ]
      c(lL, stats::approx(s$log10_Lambda, s$Delta, lL)$y, stats::approx(s$log10_Lambda, s$K, lL)$y) }, numeric(3)))
    ok = is.finite(at[, 1]); if (sum(ok) < 2) return(c(NA, NA, NA, NA))
    a = alphas[ok]; at = at[ok, , drop = FALSE]
    # width falls as alpha rises, so alpha comes from the measured width; outside the table it is held at the edge
    o = order(at[, 2]); a_hat = stats::approx(at[o, 2], a[o], W, rule = 2)$y
    c(a_hat, stats::approx(a, at[, 1], a_hat)$y, stats::approx(a, at[, 3], a_hat)$y,
      as.numeric(W < min(at[, 2]) || W > max(at[, 2])))
  }
  r = t(mapply(one, X, W))
  data.frame(alpha = r[, 1], log10_Lambda = r[, 2], psi = 10^r[, 2] / sqrt(pi), K = r[, 3], alpha_at_table_edge = r[, 4] == 1)
}

# Surface-confined (adsorbed) species: surface coverage from the peak charge,
# Gamma = Q / (n F A) (mol/cm2), and the peak current of an ideal reversible surface wave,
# ip = n^2 F^2 v A Gamma / (4 R T) (Bard and Faulkner), used as a check.
surface_coverage = function(Q_C, n = 1, area_cm2) Q_C / (n * F_const * area_cm2)
ip_surface = function(Gamma_mol_cm2, v_V_s, n = 1, area_cm2, T_K = 298.15) n^2 * F_const^2 * v_V_s * area_cm2 * Gamma_mol_cm2 / (4 * R_const * T_K)
# Laviron plot at high scan rates: Epc against log10 v has slope -2.303 RT/(alpha n F) and
# Epa slope 2.303 RT/((1 - alpha) n F) (Laviron, J. Electroanal. Chem. 1979, 101, 19, eqs. 20 and 21). ks from
# eq. 22 of the same paper, valid for n dEp above 200 mV (checked against the paper; it writes 2.3 for ln 10):
# log ks = alpha log(1 - alpha) + (1 - alpha) log alpha - log(RT / n F v) - alpha (1 - alpha) n F dEp / (2.303 RT)
laviron = function(v_V_s, Epa_V, Epc_V, n = 1, T_K = 298.15, min_dEp_mV = 200 / n) {
  k = abs(Epa_V - Epc_V) * 1000 >= min_dEp_mV
  if (sum(k) < 2) return(NULL)
  lv = log10(v_V_s[k]); sc = unname(stats::coef(stats::lm(Epc_V[k] ~ lv))[2]); sa = unname(stats::coef(stats::lm(Epa_V[k] ~ lv))[2])
  g = 2.303 * R_const * T_K / (n * F_const)
  alpha = -g / sc                                     # from the cathodic slope
  alpha_a = 1 - g / sa                                # from the anodic slope, for comparison
  vmax = max(v_V_s[k]); dE = abs(Epa_V - Epc_V)[k][which.max(v_V_s[k])]
  logks = alpha * log10(1 - alpha) + (1 - alpha) * log10(alpha) - log10(R_const * T_K / (n * F_const * vmax)) -
          alpha * (1 - alpha) * n * F_const * dE / (2.303 * R_const * T_K)
  data.frame(points = sum(k), slope_cathodic_V = sc, slope_anodic_V = sa, alpha_cathodic = alpha, alpha_anodic = alpha_a,
             ks_per_s = if (alpha > 0 && alpha < 1) 10^logks else NA)
}

# Chronoamperometry
# Cottrell: i = n F A C D^1/2 / (pi t)^1/2 (Bard and Faulkner). The slope of i against
# t^-1/2 over the chosen time window gives D (area known) or the area (D known).
cottrell_fit = function(x, t_from, t_to, n = 1, C_mM, D_cm2_s = NA, area_cm2 = NA) {
  d = x$data; k = d$t_s >= t_from & d$t_s <= t_to & d$t_s > 0
  if (sum(k) < 5) return(NULL)
  m = stats::lm(abs(d$I_A[k]) ~ I(1 / sqrt(d$t_s[k])))
  s = unname(stats::coef(m)[2]); C = mM_to_mol_cm3(C_mM)
  data.frame(file = x$file, from_s = t_from, to_s = t_to, points = sum(k), slope_A_s05 = s, intercept_A = unname(stats::coef(m)[1]),
             r2 = summary(m)$r.squared,
             D_cm2_s = if (!is.na(area_cm2)) pi * (s / (n * F_const * area_cm2 * C))^2 else NA,
             area_cm2 = if (!is.na(D_cm2_s)) s * sqrt(pi) / (n * F_const * C * sqrt(D_cm2_s)) else NA)
}
# Steady-state current at a microelectrode: disk 4 n F D C r (Saito), hemisphere and
# sphere 2 pi n F D C r and 4 pi n F D C r (Bard and Faulkner). Solves for whichever of
# D, C or r is NA.
ume_factor = function(geometry = c("disk", "hemisphere", "sphere")) switch(match.arg(geometry), disk = 4, hemisphere = 2 * pi, sphere = 4 * pi)
ume_steady = function(i_ss_A, n = 1, D_cm2_s = NA, C_mM = NA, r_cm = NA, geometry = "disk") {
  g = ume_factor(geometry); i = abs(i_ss_A); C = mM_to_mol_cm3(C_mM)
  data.frame(i_ss_A = i,
             D_cm2_s = if (is.na(D_cm2_s)) i / (g * n * F_const * C * r_cm) else D_cm2_s,
             C_mM = if (is.na(C_mM)) i / (g * n * F_const * D_cm2_s * r_cm) * 1e6 else C_mM,
             r_um = if (is.na(r_cm)) i / (g * n * F_const * D_cm2_s * C) * 1e4 else r_cm * 1e4)
}

# Chronocoulometry (Anson plot)
# Q = 2 n F A C D^1/2 t^1/2 / pi^1/2 + Q_dl + n F A Gamma (Anson; Microchim. Acta 2023,
# eq. 1). The slope gives D or A; the intercept minus the blank intercept (Q_dl, from the
# same step in electrolyte alone) gives the adsorbed amount Gamma.
anson_fit = function(x, t_from, t_to, n = 1, C_mM, D_cm2_s = NA, area_cm2 = NA, Q_dl_C = NA) {
  d = x$data
  q = if (!is.null(d$Q_C)) d$Q_C else c(0, cumsum(diff(d$t_s) * (d$I_A[-1] + d$I_A[-nrow(d)]) / 2))
  k = d$t_s >= t_from & d$t_s <= t_to
  if (sum(k) < 5) return(NULL)
  m = stats::lm(abs(q[k]) ~ sqrt(d$t_s[k]))
  s = unname(stats::coef(m)[2]); b = unname(stats::coef(m)[1]); C = mM_to_mol_cm3(C_mM)
  A = if (!is.na(area_cm2)) area_cm2 else if (!is.na(D_cm2_s)) s * sqrt(pi) / (2 * n * F_const * C * sqrt(D_cm2_s)) else NA
  data.frame(file = x$file, from_s = t_from, to_s = t_to, points = sum(k), slope_C_per_s05 = s, intercept_C = b, r2 = summary(m)$r.squared,
             D_cm2_s = if (!is.na(area_cm2)) pi * (s / (2 * n * F_const * area_cm2 * C))^2 else NA,
             area_cm2 = A,
             Gamma_mol_cm2 = if (!is.na(Q_dl_C) && !is.na(A)) (b - Q_dl_C) / (n * F_const * A) else NA)
}

# Rotating disk electrode
rpm_to_omega = function(rpm) 2 * pi * rpm / 60
# limiting current against omega^1/2: the slope gives D (or n, when D is given)
levich_fit = function(rpm, i_L_A, n = 1, area_cm2, C_mM, nu_cm2_s = 0.01, D_cm2_s = NA) {
  w = sqrt(rpm_to_omega(rpm)); m = stats::lm(abs(i_L_A) ~ w); s = unname(stats::coef(m)[2])
  k = 0.620 * F_const * area_cm2 * nu_cm2_s^(-1 / 6) * mM_to_mol_cm3(C_mM)
  data.frame(rates = length(rpm), slope_A_per_rad05 = s, intercept_A = unname(stats::coef(m)[1]), r2 = summary(m)$r.squared,
             D_cm2_s = (s / (n * k))^(3 / 2), n_from_slope = if (!is.na(D_cm2_s)) s / (k * D_cm2_s^(2 / 3)) else NA)
}
# Koutecky-Levich: 1/i = 1/i_k + 1/(B omega^1/2). Intercept gives the kinetic current
# i_k, the slope 1/B gives n when D, C, A and nu are known (or D when n is known).
koutecky_levich = function(rpm, i_A, n = NA, area_cm2, C_mM, nu_cm2_s = 0.01, D_cm2_s = NA) {
  x = 1 / sqrt(rpm_to_omega(rpm)); y = 1 / abs(i_A); m = stats::lm(y ~ x)
  s = unname(stats::coef(m)[2]); b = unname(stats::coef(m)[1])
  k = 0.620 * F_const * area_cm2 * nu_cm2_s^(-1 / 6) * mM_to_mol_cm3(C_mM)
  data.frame(rates = length(rpm), slope = s, intercept = b, r2 = summary(m)$r.squared, i_k_A = 1 / b,
             n = if (!is.na(D_cm2_s)) 1 / (s * k * D_cm2_s^(2 / 3)) else NA,
             D_cm2_s = if (!is.na(n)) (1 / (s * k * n))^(3 / 2) else NA)
}
# RRDE, oxygen reduction: electron number and peroxide yield from the disk and ring
# currents and the collection efficiency N:
# n = 4 |I_D| / (|I_D| + |I_R| / N), H2O2 % = 200 (|I_R| / N) / (|I_D| + |I_R| / N)
rrde_n_peroxide = function(I_disk_A, I_ring_A, N) {
  d = abs(I_disk_A); r = abs(I_ring_A) / N
  data.frame(n = 4 * d / (d + r), H2O2_pct = 200 * r / (d + r))
}

# Tafel analysis
# Tafel slope b (V/decade) = 2.303 R T / (alpha n F), so alpha n = 2.303 R T / (b F).
# The exchange current is the Tafel line extrapolated to the equilibrium potential.
tafel_kinetics = function(slope_dec_per_V, intercept_log10_A, E_eq_V = NA, area_cm2 = NA, T_K = 298.15) {
  b = 1 / slope_dec_per_V                                   # the fit is log10 I against E
  i0 = if (!is.na(E_eq_V)) 10^(intercept_log10_A + slope_dec_per_V * E_eq_V) else NA
  data.frame(tafel_mV_dec = 1000 * abs(b), alpha_n = 2.303 * R_const * T_K / (abs(b) * F_const),
             i0_A = i0, j0_A_cm2 = i0 / area_cm2)
}

# Probe diffusion coefficients used in the literature for electroactive-area work
redox_probes = data.frame(
  key = c("ferri", "ruhex", "other"),
  label = c("Ferricyanide, 7.6e-6 cm2/s", "Hexaammineruthenium(III), 9.1e-6 cm2/s", "Other (enter D)"),
  D_cm2_s = c(7.6e-6, 9.1e-6, NA),
