name: R/explore.R
content:
# Exploration of current-time traces: a quality check of each file, the window of a trace shown in the zoom, events
# counted over time, and the comparison of files with a reference (for example a blank). These describe the data and
# help to judge the automatic results. They do not change any result.

# Indexes of the points of a sorted time vector between a and b
trace_window = function(t, a, b) {
  i = findInterval(c(a, b), t); lo = max(1, i[1]); hi = min(length(t), max(lo, i[2]))
  lo:hi
}

# Bin medians of a current trace: n_bins equal bins of points (the median keeps spikes out); returns time and current
bin_medians = function(t, I, n_bins = 300) {
  n = length(t); b = max(1, floor(n / n_bins)); nb = floor(n / b)
  M = matrix(I[seq_len(nb * b)], nrow = b)
  list(t = t[(seq_len(nb) - 1) * b + ceiling(b / 2)], I = apply(M, 2, stats::median), b = b, nb = nb, M = M)
}

# One row per file: what was recorded and whether it looks sound before any analysis
#   noise       robust SD of the current about local medians (bins of about 1000 points), so steps, drift and spikes do not count
#   net change  median of the last 1% minus the median of the first 1% of the trace
#   gaps        steps in time longer than 1.5 x the usual sampling interval
#   at limit    share of points equal to the largest or the smallest value: a flat top or bottom suggests a clipped
#               (saturated) amplifier or a range set too small
file_check = function(x) {
  d = x$data; t = d$t_s; I = d$I_A; n = length(t)
  dts = diff(t); dt = stats::median(dts)
  bm = bin_medians(t, I, max(1, min(n %/% 1000, 3000)))
  cols = unique(round(seq(1, bm$nb, length.out = min(bm$nb, 300))))
  res = bm$M[, cols, drop = FALSE] - rep(bm$I[cols], each = nrow(bm$M))
  noise = 1.4826 * stats::median(abs(res - stats::median(res)))
  k = max(1, n %/% 100); first = stats::median(I[seq_len(k)]); last = stats::median(I[(n - k + 1):n])
  at_limit = max(mean(I == max(I)), mean(I == min(I)))
  p = x$params
  data.frame(file = x$file, points = n, duration_s = t[n] - t[1], sampling_Hz = round(1 / dt, 6),
             min_A = min(I), max_A = max(I), noise_A = noise, net_change_A = last - first, gaps = sum(dts > 1.5 * dt),
             at_limit_pct = 100 * at_limit, E_V = if (!is.null(p$E_V)) p$E_V else NA_real_,
             filter_Hz = if (!is.null(p$filter_Hz)) p$filter_Hz else NA_real_, check.names = FALSE)
}

# Plain-language notes for the file check: only what was found
file_check_notes = function(fc) {
  out = character(0)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(fc))) {
    r = fc[i, ]
    if (r$gaps > 0) out = c(out, sprintf("%s: %d gap(s) in time, longer than 1.5 times the sampling interval.", r$file, r$gaps))
    if (r$at_limit_pct > 0.1) out = c(out, sprintf("%s: %.2f%% of points sit at the largest or smallest value. The current may have been clipped (amplifier range too small).", r$file, r$at_limit_pct))
    if (!is.na(r$filter_Hz) && r$filter_Hz > 0 && r$sampling_Hz < 2.5 * r$filter_Hz)
      out = c(out, sprintf("%s: sampled at %.3g Hz, less than 2.5 times the %.3g Hz filter.", r$file, r$sampling_Hz, r$filter_Hz))
  }
  out
}

# Events (spike or step times) counted in bins of bin_s over the trace
event_rate = function(times, t0, t1, bin_s = 10) {
  br = seq(t0, t0 + max(1, ceiling((t1 - t0) / bin_s - 1e-9)) * bin_s, by = bin_s)   # whole bins from t0, the last one ending at or just after t1
  h = graphics::hist(times[times >= t0 & times <= t1], breaks = br, plot = FALSE)
  data.frame(t_mid_s = h$mids, count = h$counts, rate_per_s = h$counts / bin_s)
}

# Several traces on a common time grid (bin means over the time all files share), each optionally shifted to start at
# zero, and each minus a reference file. Bin means keep the comparison of levels; spikes are averaged within a bin.
compare_traces = function(xs, ref = 1, n_bins = 1000, start_zero = FALSE) {
  t0 = max(vapply(xs, function(x) min(x$data$t_s), 0)); t1 = min(vapply(xs, function(x) max(x$data$t_s), 0))
  if (!(t1 > t0)) stop("the files share no time range")
  br = seq(t0, t1, length.out = n_bins + 1); mid = (br[-1] + br[-length(br)]) / 2
  m = lapply(xs, function(x) { k = trace_window(x$data$t_s, t0, t1); g = findInterval(x$data$t_s[k], br, rightmost.closed = TRUE)
    v = rep(NA_real_, n_bins); s = tapply(x$data$I_A[k], g, mean); v[as.integer(names(s))] = s; v[seq_len(n_bins)] })
  if (start_zero) m = lapply(m, function(v) v - v[which(!is.na(v))[1]])
  d = do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(xs), function(i) data.frame(file = xs[[i]]$file, t_s = mid, I_A = m[[i]], diff_A = m[[i]] - m[[ref]])))
  d
}

name: R/methods.R
content:
# Analyses for voltammetry, amperometry, open-circuit potential, chronopotentiometry
# and rotating ring-disk electrodes. Every function takes a file read by read_echem()
# (or read_chi_txt / read_pine_txt) and returns plain data frames, so the app, the
# report and the tests all use the same numbers.
# Currents are in A, potentials in V, times in s, charges in C, concentrations in the
# user's unit (whatever the file names or the table say).

F_const = 96485.33212

# Concentration from file names
# Suggests a concentration for each file of a series; the user confirms it in a table.
# "+ 50mM EtOH" gives 50 (the analyte added to the electrolyte). Without a "+", a name
# with a single concentration gives that one. A file with no added concentration in a
# series where the others have one is taken as the blank (0). Anything else is NA.
conc_from_name = function(names, unit = "mM") {
  to = c(M = 1, mM = 1e-3, uM = 1e-6, nM = 1e-9)
  # units are matched in any case, because instruments often save names in lower case
  # ("5mm etoh" is 5 mM)
  canon = c(m = "M", mm = "mM", um = "uM", nm = "nM")
  one = function(n) {
    n = gsub("µ|μ", "u", n)
    pat = "[0-9]*\\.?[0-9]+(e-?[0-9]+)?\\s*([mun]?[mM])\\b"
    hit = regmatches(n, gregexpr(pat, n, ignore.case = TRUE))[[1]]
    plus = regmatches(n, regexpr(paste0("\\+\\s*", pat), n, ignore.case = TRUE))
    pick = if (length(plus)) sub("^\\+\\s*", "", plus) else if (length(hit) == 1) hit else NA
    if (is.na(pick)) return(c(value = NA, plus = length(plus) > 0))
    v = as.numeric(sub("\\s*[A-Za-z]+$", "", pick)); u = canon[[tolower(sub("^.*?([A-Za-z]+)$", "\\1", pick))]]
    c(value = v * to[[u]] / to[[unit]], plus = length(plus) > 0)
  }
  r = t(vapply(names, one, c(value = 0, plus = 0)))
  v = r[, "value"]
  # in a series where the analyte is written as "+ x", a file without "+" is the blank
  if (any(r[, "plus"] == 1)) v[r[, "plus"] == 0] = 0
  unname(v)
}
rpm_from_name = function(names) as.numeric(sub(".*?([0-9]+)\\s*rpm.*", "\\1", ifelse(grepl("[0-9]\\s*rpm", names, ignore.case = TRUE), names, NA), ignore.case = TRUE))

# Straight-line calibration with the metrics journals report: slope, intercept, R2,
# n, range, and a detection limit from the blank SD (3.3 s/slope, ICH Q2) when blank
# replicates exist, otherwise from the residual SD of the line.
calibration_line = function(conc, y, from = -Inf, to = Inf, blank_sd = NA) {
  k = !is.na(conc) & !is.na(y) & conc > 0 & conc >= from & conc <= to
  if (sum(k) < 3) return(NULL)
  m = stats::lm(y[k] ~ conc[k])
  s = unname(stats::coef(m)[2])
  s_yx = summary(m)$sigma
  data.frame(n = sum(k), from = min(conc[k]), to = max(conc[k]), slope = s,
             slope_se = summary(m)$coefficients[2, 2], intercept = unname(stats::coef(m)[1]),
             r2 = summary(m)$r.squared,
             lod = if (!is.na(blank_sd)) 3.3 * blank_sd / abs(s) else 3.3 * s_yx / abs(s),
             lod_basis = if (!is.na(blank_sd)) "3.3 x blank SD / slope" else "3.3 x residual SD / slope")
}

# Cyclic voltammetry
# Monotonic sweeps of a CV: start and end rows and direction
cv_sweeps = function(E) {
  d = sign(diff(E)); d[d == 0] = 1
  cuts = which(diff(d) != 0) + 1
  b = c(1, cuts, length(E))
  data.frame(from = b[-length(b)], to = b[-1], dir = ifelse(E[b[-1]] < E[b[-length(b)]], "cathodic", "anodic"))
}
# The last full sweep in one direction (spanning more than min_span V), which is the
# most stable cycle of a repeated CV
last_sweep = function(x, dir = "cathodic", min_span = 0.5) {
  E = x$data$E_V; I = x$data$I_A
  s = cv_sweeps(E)
  s = s[s$dir == dir & abs(E[s$to] - E[s$from]) > min_span, ]
  if (!nrow(s)) stop("No ", dir, " sweep longer than ", min_span, " V in ", x$file)
  r = s[nrow(s), ]
  data.frame(E_V = E[r$from:r$to], I_A = I[r$from:r$to])
}
# Charge of a peak between two potentials on one sweep, above a straight baseline
# joining the two window ends: Q = |integral of (I - baseline) dE| / scan rate
peak_charge = function(sweep, window, v) {
  w = sweep[sweep$E_V >= min(window) & sweep$E_V <= max(window), ]
  base = stats::approx(c(w$E_V[1], w$E_V[nrow(w)]), c(w$I_A[1], w$I_A[nrow(w)]), xout = w$E_V)$y
  net = w$I_A - base
  q = abs(sum(diff(w$E_V) * (net[-1] + net[-length(net)]) / 2)) / v
  list(Q_C = q, window = cbind(w, base_A = base))
}
# Surface area from a reduction peak with a known charge density: gold oxide 390,
# PdO 405 (uC/cm2), or any other value the user enters
ecsa_window = function(x, window, q_ref_uC_cm2, geometric_area_cm2 = NA, dir = "cathodic") {
  v = x$params$scan_rate_V_s
  s = last_sweep(x, dir)
  pc = peak_charge(s, window, v)
  ecsa = pc$Q_C / (q_ref_uC_cm2 * 1e-6)
  list(result = data.frame(file = x$file, scan_rate_V_s = v, window = sprintf("%.3f to %.3f V", min(window), max(window)),
                           Q_uC = pc$Q_C * 1e6, q_ref_uC_cm2 = q_ref_uC_cm2, ECSA_cm2 = ecsa,
                           roughness_factor = ecsa / geometric_area_cm2),
       sweep = s, window = pc$window)
}
# Peak current against scan rate for both peaks, before the log-log slope: straight-line fits of |ip| against v
# (linear for a surface-confined species) and against v^1/2 (linear through the origin for a diffusing species),
# each with slope, intercept, their standard errors and R2, then the log-log slope (0.5 for diffusion, 1 for an
# adsorbed species). Needs at least 3 scan rates for each peak.
scan_rate_fits = function(v, ipa_A, ipc_A) {
  one = function(peak, y) {
    ok = is.finite(v) & is.finite(y) & v > 0 & y != 0; vv = v[ok]; yy = abs(y[ok])
    if (length(unique(vv)) < 3) return(NULL)
    lin = function(x, against) { m = stats::lm(yy ~ x); cf = summary(m)$coefficients
      data.frame(peak = peak, against = against, n = length(yy), slope = cf[2, 1], slope_se = cf[2, 2],
                 slope_unit = if (against == "v") "A s/V" else "A (s/V)^1/2",
                 intercept_A = cf[1, 1], intercept_se_A = cf[1, 2], intercept_pct_of_smallest_ip = 100 * cf[1, 1] / min(yy), r2 = summary(m)$r.squared) }
    ll = stats::lm(log10(yy) ~ log10(vv)); cl = summary(ll)$coefficients
    list(fits = rbind(lin(vv, "v"), lin(sqrt(vv), "√v")),
         loglog = data.frame(peak = peak, n = length(yy), loglog_slope = cl[2, 1], loglog_slope_se = cl[2, 2], r2 = summary(ll)$r.squared))
  }
  r = Filter(Negate(is.null), list(one("anodic", ipa_A), one("cathodic", ipc_A)))
  if (!length(r)) return(NULL)
  list(fits = do.call(rbind, lapply(r, `[[`, "fits")), loglog = do.call(rbind, lapply(r, `[[`, "loglog")))
}
# What the scan-rate fits point to, one line per peak: which value the log-log slope is closer to, and the intercept of
# the line against v^1/2 as a share of the smallest peak current. It is flagged when it differs from zero by more than
# 2 standard errors and is larger than 5% of the smallest peak (a default of this app, not a published criterion);
# with noise-free data the standard error alone would flag intercepts of a few parts per million.
scan_rate_reading = function(sf) {
  if (is.null(sf)) return("At least 3 scan rates are needed for each peak.")
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(sf$loglog)), function(i) { L = sf$loglog[i, ]; q = sf$fits[sf$fits$peak == L$peak & sf$fits$against == "√v", ]
    sprintf("%s peak: log-log slope %.3f ± %.3f, closer to %s. Against √v the intercept is %s.",
            tools::toTitleCase(L$peak), L$loglog_slope, L$loglog_slope_se,
            if (L$loglog_slope < 0.75) "0.5 (diffusion-controlled)" else "1 (surface-confined species)",
            if (abs(q$intercept_A) <= 2 * q$intercept_se_A || abs(q$intercept_pct_of_smallest_ip) <= 5)
              sprintf("%.2g%% of the smallest peak, close to zero as expected for diffusion", q$intercept_pct_of_smallest_ip)
            else sprintf("%.3g µA (%.2g%% of the smallest peak): charging current, background or slow kinetics may contribute", q$intercept_A * 1e6, q$intercept_pct_of_smallest_ip))
  }, "")
}
# Tafel slope over one potential window of a slow LSV. Because the answer depends on
# the window, tafel_scan() fits every window of a few widths so the choice is visible.
tafel_fit = function(x, window) {
  d = x$data; k = d$E_V >= min(window) & d$E_V <= max(window) & d$I_A > 0
  if (sum(k) < 3) return(NULL)
  m = stats::lm(log10(d$I_A[k]) ~ d$E_V[k])
  s = unname(stats::coef(m)[2])
  data.frame(from_V = min(window), to_V = max(window), n = sum(k), tafel_mV_dec = 1000 / s, r2 = summary(m)$r.squared)
}
tafel_scan = function(x, from = min(x$data$E_V), to = max(x$data$E_V), widths = c(0.006, 0.020, 0.050), step = 0.002, min_r2 = 0.99) {
  out = do.call(rbind, lapply(widths, function(w) do.call(rbind, lapply(seq(from, to - w, by = step), function(lo) {
    t = tafel_fit(x, c(lo, lo + w)); if (!is.null(t)) cbind(width_mV = w * 1000, t) }))))
  if (is.null(out)) return(NULL)
  out[out$r2 > min_r2 & out$tafel_mV_dec > 0 & out$tafel_mV_dec < 400, ]
}

# Pulse voltammetry (DPV, SWV)
# The response of one voltammogram: the current at a set potential (nearest point), or
# the largest current within a potential window
pulse_response = function(x, mode = c("at_potential", "peak"), E_read = NA, window = NULL) {
  mode = match.arg(mode); d = x$data
  if (mode == "at_potential") { k = which.min(abs(d$E_V - E_read)); return(data.frame(file = x$file, E_V = d$E_V[k], I_A = d$I_A[k])) }
  w = d[d$E_V >= min(window) & d$E_V <= max(window), ]
  k = which.max(abs(w$I_A))
  data.frame(file = x$file, E_V = w$E_V[k], I_A = w$I_A[k])
}

# Open-circuit potential
ocp_summary = function(x, last_s = 60) {
  d = x$data; tail_ = d[d$t_s >= max(d$t_s) - last_s, ]
  drift = unname(stats::coef(stats::lm(tail_$E_V ~ tail_$t_s))[2]) * 1000 * 60
  data.frame(file = x$file, run_s = max(d$t_s), E_end_V = d$E_V[nrow(d)], E_min_V = min(d$E_V), E_max_V = max(d$E_V),
             E_mean_last_V = mean(tail_$E_V), drift_last_mV_min = drift)
}

# Chronoamperometry
# Charge passed in an i-t record (for example a deposition step), and the same charge
# expressed as monolayers when an area and a monolayer charge density are given
charge_passed = function(x, area_cm2 = NA, q_ml_uC_cm2 = NA) {
  d = x$data
  q = abs(sum(diff(d$t_s) * (d$I_A[-1] + d$I_A[-nrow(d)]) / 2))
  data.frame(file = x$file, E_V = chi_setting(x, "Init E (V)"), time_s = max(d$t_s), Q_uC = q * 1e6,
             I_start_uA = d$I_A[1] * 1e6, I_end_uA = mean(utils::tail(d$I_A, 100)) * 1e6,
             monolayers = q / (q_ml_uC_cm2 * 1e-6 * area_cm2))
}
# Mean current over the last avg_s seconds before each time in t_ends
current_at_ends = function(d, t_ends, avg_s) vapply(t_ends, function(te) {
  k = d$t_s > te - avg_s & d$t_s <= te
  if (any(k)) mean(d$I_A[k]) else NA_real_
}, 0)
# Step chronoamperometry (CHI "Chronoamperometry", one or two steps of equal width):
# the current at the end of each step
step_currents = function(x, avg_s = 2) {
  w = chi_setting(x, "Pulse Width (sec)"); n = chi_setting(x, "Step", 1)
  i = current_at_ends(x$data, w * seq_len(n), avg_s)
  stats::setNames(data.frame(x$file, t(i)), c("file", paste0("I_step", seq_len(n), "_A")))
}
# Multi-potential steps (CHI "Multi-Potential Steps"): steps E1, T1, E2, T2, ... repeated
# for a number of cycles. The response is the current at the end of the sensing step
# (by default the last step) in each cycle. The first cycle is left out of the mean
# because the surface is still changing; the spread over the others gives the RSD.
multistep_currents = function(x, sense_step = NULL, avg_s = 1, skip_cycles = 1) {
  st = x$params$settings
  k = sort(as.integer(sub("^E([0-9]+) \\(V\\)$", "\\1", grep("^E[0-9]+ \\(V\\)$", names(st), value = TRUE))))
  E = vapply(k, function(j) st[[sprintf("E%d (V)", j)]], 0)
  Tt = vapply(k, function(j) st[[sprintf("T%d (s)", j)]], 0)
  n = chi_setting(x, "Cycle", 1)
  if (is.null(sense_step)) sense_step = length(k)
  per = sum(Tt)
  ends = (seq_len(n) - 1) * per + sum(Tt[seq_len(sense_step)])
  i = current_at_ends(x$data, ends, avg_s)
  use = i[-seq_len(min(skip_cycles, n - 1))]
  data.frame(file = x$file, sense_E_V = E[sense_step], steps = paste(sprintf("%g V %g s", E, Tt), collapse = ", "),
             cycles = n, I_mean_A = mean(use), I_sd_A = if (length(use) > 1) stats::sd(use) else NA,
             rsd_pct = if (length(use) > 1) 100 * stats::sd(use) / abs(mean(use)) else NA,
             I_cycles = paste(signif(i, 4), collapse = "; "))
}

# Chronopotentiometry
# Transition time. At the start the potential moves fast while the double layer charges
# and the surface reaches the redox couple; it then slows on the plateau of the couple,
# and moves fast again at the transition, when the couple is used up at the surface.
# The transition is therefore the steepest point that comes after the slope has dipped:
# a point counts only if its slope is at least rise times the lowest slope before it.
# When the plateau is too short to separate from the start, no transition is reported.
# The run must also have settled afterwards (end slope below a tenth of the transition
# slope). E at tau/4 is the quarter-wave potential, close to E1/2 for a reversible couple.
#
# The default (steepest point) matches the usual reading of tau as the point of greatest
# slope (Pine Research, chronopotentiometry support article). method = "tangent" is a
# tangent-intersection construction written for comparison; no published procedure for it
# has been checked yet, so treat it as an alternative reading, not a reference method.
# It draws a tangent on the plateau (at its
# flattest point before the inflection) and a tangent at the inflection; tau is the time
# where they cross, which marks the start of the transition and so comes earlier than
# the inflection. The time where the inflection tangent crosses a tangent on the flattest
# part after the transition (within three inflection times) is given as tau_end.
cp_transition = function(x, skip_s = 0.3, smooth_s = 0.5, rise = 1.1, min_step_V = 0.05, method = c("inflection", "tangent")) {
  method = match.arg(method)
  d = x$data[!duplicated(x$data$t_s), ]
  dt = stats::median(diff(d$t_s)); k = max(3, round(smooth_s / dt))
  Es = stats::filter(d$E_V, rep(1 / k, k), sides = 2)
  s = abs(c(NA, diff(Es)) / dt)
  use = which(d$t_s > skip_s & !is.na(s))
  low_before = cummin(s[use])
  cand = use[s[use] >= rise * low_before]
  i_app = abs(chi_setting(x, "Cathodic Current (A)", NA))
  j = if (length(cand)) cand[which.max(s[cand])] else NA
  end_slope = mean(utils::tail(s[!is.na(s)], k))
  # a real transition moves the potential by tens of mV between tau/2 and 2 tau; a bump
  # in a slow drift does not
  step = if (is.na(j)) 0 else abs(diff(stats::approx(d$t_s, d$E_V, c(d$t_s[j] / 2, min(2 * d$t_s[j], max(d$t_s))))$y))
  ok = !is.na(j) && end_slope < 0.1 * s[j] && d$t_s[j] < 0.9 * max(d$t_s) && step >= min_step_V
  tau = if (ok) d$t_s[j] else NA
  tau_end = NA
  if (ok && method == "tangent") {
    sg = c(NA, diff(Es)) / dt                         # signed slope of the smoothed curve
    line = function(i) c(a = Es[i] - sg[i] * d$t_s[i], b = sg[i])
    cross = function(L1, L2) unname((L2["a"] - L1["a"]) / (L1["b"] - L2["b"]))
    pre = which(d$t_s > skip_s & d$t_s < d$t_s[j] & !is.na(sg))
    post = which(d$t_s > d$t_s[j] & d$t_s <= 3 * d$t_s[j] & !is.na(sg))
    Lj = line(j)
    tau = cross(line(pre[which.min(abs(sg[pre]))]), Lj)
    if (length(post)) tau_end = cross(Lj, line(post[which.min(abs(sg[post]))]))
  }
  data.frame(file = x$file, method = method, current_A = i_app, run_s = max(d$t_s), tau_s = tau, tau_end_s = tau_end,
             E_at_tau_V = if (ok) stats::approx(d$t_s, d$E_V, tau)$y else NA,
             E_quarter_V = if (ok) stats::approx(d$t_s, d$E_V, tau / 4)$y else NA,
             step_mV = 1000 * step,
             note = if (ok) "" else if (is.na(j)) "no separate transition: the plateau is too short to tell it from the start of the run"
                    else if (step < min_step_V) "no clear transition: no sharp potential step after the plateau"
                    else "no clear transition: the potential had not settled again by the end of the run")
}
# Sand equation: i tau^1/2 / C is constant for a diffusion-controlled process. With the
# electrode area, D follows from i tau^1/2 = n F A C (pi D)^1/2 / 2.
sand_table = function(tr, conc_mM, n = 1, area_cm2 = NA) {
  C = conc_mM * 1e-6                                  # mol/cm3
  it = tr$current_A * sqrt(tr$tau_s)
  cbind(tr[, c("file", "current_A", "tau_s")], conc_mM = conc_mM, i_sqrt_tau = it, i_sqrt_tau_per_C = it / conc_mM,
        D_cm2_s = (2 * it / (n * F_const * area_cm2 * C))^2 / pi)
}
# Sand line across concentrations: i tau^1/2 against C. A non-zero intercept points to
# a contribution that does not scale with concentration (double-layer charging,
# adsorption), which is why D is taken from the slope rather than from single files.
sand_fit = function(tab, n = 1, area_cm2 = NA) {
  k = !is.na(tab$tau_s) & !is.na(tab$conc_mM)
  if (sum(k) < 2) return(NULL)
  m = stats::lm(tab$i_sqrt_tau[k] ~ tab$conc_mM[k])
  s = unname(stats::coef(m)[2])                         # A s^1/2 per mM
  data.frame(n_files = sum(k), slope_A_s05_per_mM = s, intercept_A_s05 = unname(stats::coef(m)[1]),
             r2 = summary(m)$r.squared,
             D_from_slope_cm2_s = (2 * s / (n * F_const * area_cm2 * 1e-6))^2 / pi)
}

# Rotating ring-disk electrode
# Collection efficiency N = -I_ring / I_disk over a disk-potential window on the
# limiting-current plateau. The two currents have opposite signs whatever the
# instrument's sign convention, so the ratio is positive.
rrde_collection = function(x, disk_window, rpm = NA) {
  d = x$data
  if (is.null(d$I2_A)) stop(x$file, " has no ring current (second channel)")
  w = d[d$E_V >= min(disk_window) & d$E_V <= max(disk_window), ]
  n = -w$I2_A / w$I_A
  data.frame(file = x$file, rpm = rpm, N = mean(n), N_sd = stats::sd(n), points = nrow(w),
             I_disk_A = mean(w$I_A), I_ring_A = mean(w$I2_A),
             ring_E_V = if (!is.null(d$E2_V)) stats::median(d$E2_V) else chi_setting(x, "2nd E (V)", NA))
}
# Levich check across rotation rates: limiting disk current against omega^1/2
levich = function(cal) {
  cal = cal[!is.na(cal$rpm), ]
  if (nrow(cal) < 2) return(NULL)
  w = sqrt(2 * pi * cal$rpm / 60)
  m = stats::lm(abs(cal$I_disk_A) ~ w)
  data.frame(n = nrow(cal), slope_A_per_rad_s = unname(stats::coef(m)[2]), intercept_A = unname(stats::coef(m)[1]),
             r2 = summary(m)$r.squared)
}
# Faradaic efficiency of a product made at the disk and collected at the ring:
# FE = |I_ring| / (N |I_disk|), point by point and averaged over a disk-potential window.
# An optional ring baseline (the ring current where the disk makes no product) is
# subtracted first.
rrde_fe = function(x, N, disk_window, ring_baseline_window = NULL) {
  d = x$data
  if (is.null(d$I2_A)) stop(x$file, " has no ring current (second channel)")
  base = if (is.null(ring_baseline_window)) 0 else
    stats::median(d$I2_A[d$E_V >= min(ring_baseline_window) & d$E_V <= max(ring_baseline_window)])
  d$FE_pct = 100 * abs(d$I2_A - base) / (N * abs(d$I_A))
  w = d[d$E_V >= min(disk_window) & d$E_V <= max(disk_window), ]
  list(summary = data.frame(file = x$file, N = N, window = sprintf("%.3f to %.3f V", min(disk_window), max(disk_window)),
                            ring_baseline_A = base, FE_mean_pct = mean(w$FE_pct), FE_sd_pct = stats::sd(w$FE_pct),
                            points = nrow(w)),
       curve = d)
}

name: R/performance.R
content:
# Sensor performance: the "S-criteria" of chemical sensors (sensitivity, selectivity, speed and stability), with
# specificity and precision, from result values of any technique.
# Each function takes a small table that the user prepares (one row per measurement) and returns plain results.
# ISE-specific methods (Nernstian slope, IUPAC selectivity methods, the check standard) stay under Potentiometry.

# Column names are matched loosely: case, spaces and units in brackets do not matter
perf_cols = function(d) { n = tolower(gsub("\\s*\\(.*\\)\\s*$", "", names(d))); names(d) = gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "_", n); d }
perf_need = function(d, cols, what) {
  miss = setdiff(cols, names(d))
  if (length(miss)) stop(sprintf("%s needs the column(s) %s (download the template to see the layout).", what, paste(miss, collapse = ", ")))
  d
}
perf_num = function(v) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(v))

# Sensitivity: the calibration slope, its linear range, LOD and LOQ. The noise s is the SD of repeated blanks
# (concentration 0) when there are at least two, otherwise the residual SD of the line (ICH Q2: LOD = 3.3 s/slope,
# LOQ = 10 s/slope). With an electrode area, the slope per unit area is given as well.
perf_sensitivity = function(d, from = -Inf, to = Inf, area_cm2 = NA) {
  d = perf_need(perf_cols(d), c("concentration", "signal"), "Sensitivity")
  conc = perf_num(d$concentration); y = perf_num(d$signal)
  blank = y[!is.na(conc) & conc == 0 & !is.na(y)]
  blank_sd = if (length(blank) >= 2) stats::sd(blank) else NA_real_
  f = calibration_line(conc, y, from, to, blank_sd)
  if (is.null(f)) stop("Sensitivity needs at least three standards above zero in the chosen range.")
  k = !is.na(conc) & !is.na(y) & conc > 0 & conc >= from & conc <= to
  s = if (!is.na(blank_sd)) blank_sd else summary(stats::lm(y[k] ~ conc[k]))$sigma
  f$loq = 10 * s / abs(f$slope)
  f$slope_per_area = if (is.finite(area_cm2) && area_cm2 > 0) f$slope / area_cm2 else NA_real_
  f$blanks = length(blank)
  list(fit = f, points = data.frame(concentration = conc, signal = y, used = k))
}

# Selectivity: the change of the analyte signal caused by each interferent (analyte alone against analyte plus
# interferent), in percent, against a tolerance the user sets. Replicates of one interferent are averaged. This is the
# second selectivity procedure of Thévenot et al., Pure Appl. Chem. 1999, 71, 2333, section 5.2: the interferent at its
# expected concentration, the analyte at the middle of its expected range.
perf_selectivity = function(d, tolerance_pct = 5) {
  d = perf_need(perf_cols(d), c("interferent", "signal_analyte", "signal_mixture"), "Selectivity")
  d$a = perf_num(d$signal_analyte); d$m = perf_num(d$signal_mixture)
  conc = if ("interferent_concentration" %in% names(d)) as.character(d$interferent_concentration) else ""
  g = paste(d$interferent, conc)
  out = do.call(rbind, lapply(split(seq_len(nrow(d)), factor(g, levels = unique(g))), function(i) {
    a = mean(d$a[i], na.rm = TRUE); m = mean(d$m[i], na.rm = TRUE)
    data.frame(interferent = d$interferent[i[1]], interferent_concentration = conc[i[1]], replicates = length(i),
               signal_analyte = a, signal_mixture = m, change_pct = 100 * (m - a) / a)
  }))
  out$within_tolerance = abs(out$change_pct) <= tolerance_pct
  out
}

# Specificity (cross-reactivity): the response to each other species alone, at the same concentration as the target, as a
# percentage of the target response, and as the ratio of the target signal to that species' signal. The ratio is the first
# selectivity procedure of Thévenot et al., Pure Appl. Chem. 1999, 71, 2333, section 5.2 (no ratio when a species gives no
# positive signal). IUPAC recommends the graded term selectivity; specificity is absolute (Vessman et al., Pure Appl. Chem. 2001, 73, 1381).
perf_specificity = function(d) {
  d = perf_need(perf_cols(d), c("species", "signal", "target"), "Specificity")
  d$y = perf_num(d$signal); tg = toupper(trimws(as.character(d$target))) %in% c("TRUE", "T", "YES", "Y", "1")
  if (!any(tg)) stop("Specificity: mark the target species with yes in the target column.")
  ref = mean(d$y[tg], na.rm = TRUE)
  out = do.call(rbind, lapply(split(seq_len(nrow(d)), factor(d$species, levels = unique(d$species))), function(i)
    data.frame(species = d$species[i[1]], target = any(tg[i]), replicates = length(i), signal = mean(d$y[i], na.rm = TRUE))))
  out$cross_reactivity_pct = 100 * out$signal / ref
  out$selectivity_ratio = ifelse(out$signal > 0, ref / out$signal, NA_real_)
  out
}

# Stability: the signal over time (days, hours or cycles) as a percentage of the first value, the straight-line
# change per unit time, and when the signal first falls below the retention limit (90% by default), interpolated.
perf_stability = function(d, limit_pct = 90) {
  d = perf_need(perf_cols(d), c("time", "signal"), "Stability")
  tt = perf_num(d$time); y = perf_num(d$signal); k = !is.na(tt) & !is.na(y); tt = tt[k]; y = y[k]
  m = tapply(y, tt, mean); tm = as.numeric(names(m)); m = as.numeric(m)
  if (length(m) < 2) stop("Stability needs signals at two or more times.")
  ret = 100 * m / m[1]
  fit = stats::lm(ret ~ tm)
  below = which(ret < limit_pct)
  t_limit = if (length(below)) { j = below[1]; tm[j - 1] + (limit_pct - ret[j - 1]) * (tm[j] - tm[j - 1]) / (ret[j] - ret[j - 1]) } else NA_real_
  list(points = data.frame(time = tm, signal = m, retention_pct = ret),
       summary = data.frame(times = length(m), retained_at_last_pct = ret[length(ret)], change_pct_per_unit = unname(stats::coef(fit)[2]),
                            first_time_below_limit = t_limit, limit_pct = limit_pct, last_time = max(tm)))
}

# Speed: the response time after an addition at t_add. Baseline = median over pre_s before the addition, final level
# = median over the last post_s of the trace; the trace is smoothed with a running median over smooth_s, and t90 (t95)
# is the first time after the addition at which it has covered 90% (95%) of the change.
perf_speed = function(t, y, t_add, pre_s = 2, post_s = 10, smooth_s = 0.2) {
  o = order(t); t = t[o]; y = y[o]
  dt = stats::median(diff(t[seq_len(min(length(t), 10000))])); w = max(1, 2 * floor(smooth_s / dt / 2) + 1)
  ys = if (w > 1 && w < length(y)) as.numeric(stats::runmed(y, w, endrule = "median")) else y
  base = stats::median(y[t >= t_add - pre_s & t < t_add]); fin = stats::median(y[t >= max(t) - post_s])
  if (!is.finite(base) || !is.finite(fin)) stop("Speed: no points in the baseline or final window. Check the addition time.")
  ch = fin - base; after = t > t_add
  cross = function(f) { lev = base + f * ch; i = which(after & (if (ch > 0) ys >= lev else ys <= lev))[1]; if (is.na(i)) NA_real_ else t[i] - t_add }
  data.frame(t_add_s = t_add, baseline = base, final = fin, change = ch, t90_s = cross(0.9), t95_s = cross(0.95))
}

# A trace for the speed tab: EMF16 recordings as potential (mV) of one channel; other files through the instrument
# readers, as current when the file has a current, otherwise potential (V)
perf_trace = function(path, name, instrument = "auto", channel = NULL) {
  emf = tryCatch(read_emf16_grf(path)$long, error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(emf) && nrow(emf)) {
    chs = unique(emf$channel); ch = if (isTRUE(channel %in% chs)) channel else chs[1]; e = emf[emf$channel == ch, ]
    return(list(file = name, t = e$time_s, y = e$emf_mV, label = "Potential (mV)", scale = 1, channels = chs, channel = ch))
  }
  d = read_echem(path, name, instrument)$data
  if (is.null(d$t_s)) stop(name, ": the file has no time column")
  if (!is.null(d$I_A)) { u = current_unit(d$I_A)
    list(file = name, t = d$t_s, y = d$I_A, label = paste0("Current (", u$label, ")"), scale = u$scale, channels = NULL, channel = NULL) }
  else list(file = name, t = d$t_s, y = d$E_V, label = "Potential (V)", scale = 1, channels = NULL, channel = NULL)
}

# Precision in the terms of ICH Q2(R2): repeatability (same conditions), intermediate precision (within one
# laboratory, here across days and electrodes) and reproducibility (between laboratories). Variance components from
# a linear mixed model with the grouping columns present (day, electrode, laboratory) as random effects, fitted by
# REML (lme4). Electrode-to-electrode variation, often called reproducibility in sensor papers, is part of the
# intermediate precision here; reproducibility needs results from two or more laboratories.
perf_precision = function(d, min_levels = 5) {
  d = perf_need(perf_cols(d), c("value"), "Precision")
  d$value = perf_num(d$value); d = d[!is.na(d$value), , drop = FALSE]
  groups = intersect(c("day", "electrode", "laboratory"), names(d))
  groups = groups[vapply(groups, function(g) length(unique(stats::na.omit(d[[g]]))) >= 2, TRUE)]
  for (g in groups) d[[g]] = factor(d[[g]])
  notes = character(0); sd_g = setNames(rep(NA_real_, 3), c("day", "electrode", "laboratory"))
  if (length(groups)) {
    f = stats::as.formula(paste("value ~ 1 +", paste(sprintf("(1 | %s)", groups), collapse = " + ")))
    m = suppressMessages(lme4::lmer(f, data = d, REML = TRUE))
    vc = as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(m)); rep_sd = vc$sdcor[vc$grp == "Residual"]
    for (g in groups) sd_g[[g]] = vc$sdcor[vc$grp == g]
    if (lme4::isSingular(m)) notes = c(notes, "The model is singular: at least one variance component is estimated as zero, often because there are few groups.")
    for (g in groups) if (nlevels(d[[g]]) < min_levels) notes = c(notes, sprintf("Only %d %s levels: the between-%s SD is indicative only (five or more are usually needed).", nlevels(d[[g]]), g, g))
  } else { rep_sd = stats::sd(d$value); notes = c(notes, "No day, electrode or laboratory column with two or more levels: only the repeatability is given.") }
  z = function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), 0, x)
  inter = sqrt(rep_sd^2 + z(sd_g[["day"]])^2 + z(sd_g[["electrode"]])^2)
  repro = if (!is.na(sd_g[["laboratory"]])) sqrt(inter^2 + sd_g[["laboratory"]]^2) else NA_real_
  mu = mean(d$value)
  comp = data.frame(component = c("Repeatability (within-run SD)", "Between-day SD", "Between-electrode SD", "Intermediate precision (within the laboratory)",
                                  "Between-laboratory SD", "Reproducibility (between laboratories)"),
                    SD = c(rep_sd, sd_g[["day"]], sd_g[["electrode"]], if (any(c("day", "electrode") %in% groups)) inter else NA, sd_g[["laboratory"]], repro))
  comp$RSD_pct = 100 * comp$SD / abs(mu)
  list(components = comp[!is.na(comp$SD), ], mean = mu, n = nrow(d), groups = groups, notes = notes)
}

# Templates: the columns each table needs (and the optional ones), with no example values
perf_templates = list(
  sensitivity = data.frame(concentration = numeric(0), signal = numeric(0)),
  selectivity = data.frame(interferent = character(0), interferent_concentration = character(0), signal_analyte = numeric(0), signal_mixture = numeric(0)),
  specificity = data.frame(species = character(0), signal = numeric(0), target = character(0)),
  stability = data.frame(time = numeric(0), signal = numeric(0)),
  precision = data.frame(value = numeric(0), day = character(0), electrode = character(0), laboratory = character(0)))

name: R/provenance.R
content:
# Version and provenance: what made a result. Every report carries the tool version, the R version, the time it was
# made and a checksum of every file used, and the Report tab can download all of it as one bundle (settings, file
# checksums, package versions, every results table and a copy of the code) so a result can be traced and re-run.

# Pre-release number until the first public release; raise it with every deployed change
electrofast_version = "1.0.0"
electrofast_version_date = "2026-10-21"

electrofast_packages = c("shiny", "bslib", "ggplot2", "officer", "rmarkdown", "jsonlite", "lme4", "zip", "gridExtra")
package_versions = function(pk = electrofast_packages) {
  v = vapply(pk, function(p) if (requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) as.character(utils::packageVersion(p)) else "not installed", "")
  data.frame(package = pk, version = unname(v))
}

# The uploaded files: every fileInput value is a data frame with name, size and datapath
input_files = function(inputs) {
  f = Filter(function(v) is.data.frame(v) && all(c("name", "datapath") %in% names(v)), inputs)
  if (!length(f)) return(data.frame(input = character(), file = character(), bytes = numeric(), md5 = character()))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(f), function(k) { d = f[[k]]
    data.frame(input = k, file = d$name, bytes = file.size(d$datapath), md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(d$datapath))) }))
}

# Every other setting, as text (buttons and file inputs left out)
input_settings = function(inputs) {
  s = Filter(function(v) !is.data.frame(v) && !inherits(v, "shinyActionButtonValue") && length(v) <= 50 && (is.atomic(v) || is.null(v)), inputs)
  s = s[order(names(s))]
  data.frame(input = names(s), value = vapply(s, function(v) if (is.null(v)) "" else paste(v, collapse = ", "), ""), row.names = NULL)
}

provenance_lines = function(files = NULL) c(
  `ElectroFast version` = sprintf("%s (%s)", electrofast_version, electrofast_version_date),
  `R version` = paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = "."),
  Created = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z"),
  `Files used` = if (is.null(files) || !nrow(files)) "none" else paste(sprintf("%s (md5 %s)", files$file, substr(files$md5, 1, 8)), collapse = "; "))

# The bundle: a zip with settings, file checksums, versions, every results table of the report sections and the code
build_bundle = function(zipfile, inputs, sections, code_dir = ".") {
  d = file.path(tempfile("electrofast_bundle_"), "ElectroFast_bundle"); dir.create(file.path(d, "results"), recursive = TRUE)
  files = input_files(inputs)
  utils::write.csv(input_settings(inputs), file.path(d, "settings.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  utils::write.csv(files, file.path(d, "files.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  writeLines(c(paste(names(provenance_lines(files)), provenance_lines(files), sep = ": "), "", "Packages:",
               apply(package_versions(), 1, paste, collapse = " ")), file.path(d, "versions.txt"))
  k = 0
  for (s in sections) for (nm in names(s$tables)) { t = s$tables[[nm]]; if (!is.data.frame(t)) next; k = k + 1
    fn = sprintf("%02d_%s_%s.csv", k, gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", s$title), gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", nm))
    utils::write.csv(t, file.path(d, "results", fn), row.names = FALSE) }
  dir.create(file.path(d, "code", "R"), recursive = TRUE); dir.create(file.path(d, "code", "report"))
  file.copy(list.files(code_dir, "^app.*\\.R$", full.names = TRUE), file.path(d, "code"))
  file.copy(list.files(file.path(code_dir, "R"), "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE), file.path(d, "code", "R"))
  file.copy(file.path(code_dir, "report", "electrofast_report.Rmd"), file.path(d, "code", "report"))
  writeLines(c("ElectroFast reproducibility bundle", "",
    "settings.csv   every setting in the app when the bundle was made",
    "files.csv      every uploaded file, with its size and MD5 checksum (to show the same files are used again)",
    "versions.txt   ElectroFast, R and package versions, and when the bundle was made",
    "results/       every results table in the report, as CSV",
    "code/          the app code that made the results",
    "", "To repeat the analysis:", "1. Run the app with shiny::runApp(\"code\"), or open the same ElectroFast version.",
    "2. Load the files listed in files.csv and check their MD5 sums.", "3. Enter the settings in settings.csv."), file.path(d, "README.txt"))
  old = setwd(dirname(d)); on.exit(setwd(old))
  zip::zipr(zipfile, "ElectroFast_bundle")
}

name: R/qc.R
R/read_abf.R
content:
# Axon Binary Format (.abf) files from pCLAMP / Clampex. Patch-clamp amplifiers are also used as low-noise
# potentiostats, for example for single-particle impact chronoamperometry at an ultramicroelectrode: a constant
# potential and the current recorded against time. The data are read with the readABF package (GPL-3, pure R).
# The holding potential, the amplifier filter and the protocol name, which readABF does not return, are read from
# the ABF2 header (section map at byte 76, ADC and DAC records and the strings section, as in the ABF2 layout that
# pyABF also follows). The string list is aligned on the channel units that readABF returns, so a wrong offset stops
# the read of those settings instead of giving wrong ones.

is_abf = function(path) {
  s = tryCatch(readBin(path, "raw", 4), error = function(e) raw(0))
  length(s) == 4 && rawToChar(s) %in% c("ABF2", "ABF ")
}

# current units to amperes
abf_current_scale = c(A = 1, mA = 1e-3, uA = 1e-6, "µA" = 1e-6, nA = 1e-9, pA = 1e-12, fA = 1e-15)

# Settings from an ABF2 header: telegraph filter, holding potential of DAC 0 with its units, protocol file name
abf2_settings = function(path, adc_units) {
  h = readBin(path, "raw", 65536)
  i32 = function(o) readBin(h[(o + 1):(o + 4)], "integer", size = 4, endian = "little")
  f32 = function(o) readBin(h[(o + 1):(o + 4)], "numeric", size = 4, endian = "little")
  sec = function(i) c(offset = i32(76 + 16 * i) * 512, bytes = i32(76 + 16 * i + 4), n = i32(76 + 16 * i + 8))
  adc = sec(1); dac = sec(2); str = sec(9)
  out = list(filter_Hz = f32(adc[["offset"]] + 10), lowpass_Hz = f32(adc[["offset"]] + 56), gain = f32(adc[["offset"]] + 6),
             holding = f32(dac[["offset"]] + 12), holding_units = NA_character_, protocol = NA_character_)
  # strings: the block split at zero bytes; index 1 is aligned so that the ADC units index points at the units readABF gave
  if (str[["offset"]] > 0 && str[["offset"]] + str[["bytes"]] <= length(h)) {
    b = h[(str[["offset"]] + 1):(str[["offset"]] + str[["bytes"]])]
    # split the bytes at zeros directly (the block starts with binary header bytes, which are not valid text)
    z = which(b == as.raw(0)); st0 = c(1, z + 1); en0 = c(z - 1, length(b))
    s = vapply(seq_along(st0), function(k) if (en0[k] >= st0[k]) iconv(rawToChar(b[st0[k]:en0[k]]), "latin1", "UTF-8") else "", "")
    u_idx = i32(adc[["offset"]] + 78)          # lADCUnitsIndex of ADC 0
    pos = which(s == adc_units)
    if (length(pos)) {
      off = pos[1] - u_idx
      get = function(k) if (k > 0 && off + k <= length(s)) s[off + k] else NA_character_
      out$holding_units = get(i32(dac[["offset"]] + 28))      # lDACChannelUnitsIndex of DAC 0
      p = get(i32(72))                                          # uProtocolPathIndex in the file header (byte 72)
      if (!is.na(p)) out$protocol = basename(gsub("\\\\", "/", p))
    }
  }
  out
}

# One file to the same structure as the other readers: data with t_s and I_A (and sweep when there are several),
# settings in params. The current channel is the first channel recorded in a current unit.
read_abf = function(path, name = basename(path)) {
  a = readABF::readABF(path)
  units = trimws(a$channelUnits)
  ch = which(units %in% names(abf_current_scale))[1]
  if (is.na(ch)) stop(name, ": no channel recorded in a current unit (channels: ", paste(a$channelNames, units, collapse = ", "), ")")
  dt = a$samplingIntervalInSec; sc = abf_current_scale[[units[ch]]]
  d = if (length(a$data) == 1) data.frame(t_s = (seq_len(nrow(a$data[[1]])) - 1) * dt, I_A = a$data[[1]][, ch] * sc) else
    do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(a$data), function(k) data.frame(sweep = k, t_s = (seq_len(nrow(a$data[[k]])) - 1) * dt, I_A = a$data[[k]][, ch] * sc)))
  hd = a$header
  mode = c("1" = "event-driven", "2" = "oscilloscope", "3" = "gap-free", "4" = "high-speed oscilloscope", "5" = "episodic")[as.character(hd$nOperationMode)]
  st = if (isTRUE(hd$fFileVersionNumber >= 2)) tryCatch(abf2_settings(path, units[ch]), error = function(e) NULL)
  E = if (!is.null(st) && identical(st$holding_units, "mV")) st$holding / 1000 else if (!is.null(st) && identical(st$holding_units, "V")) st$holding else NA_real_
  date = as.character(hd$uFileStartDate); ms = hd$uFileStartTimeMS
  start = if (!is.null(ms) && nchar(date) == 8) sprintf("%s-%s-%s %02d:%02d:%02d", substr(date, 1, 4), substr(date, 5, 6), substr(date, 7, 8),
                                                         ms %/% 3600000, (ms %/% 60000) %% 60, (ms %/% 1000) %% 60) else NA_character_
  list(file = name, kind = "ca", data = d,
       params = list(technique = paste("Chronoamperometry,", if (is.na(mode)) "ABF" else mode, "recording (Axon ABF)"),
                     instrument = "Axon pCLAMP", scan_rate_V_s = NA_real_, E_V = E,
                     sampling_Hz = round(1 / dt, 6), sweeps = length(a$data), channel = a$channelNames[ch], channel_units = units[ch],
                     filter_Hz = if (!is.null(st)) st$filter_Hz else NA_real_, protocol = if (!is.null(st)) st$protocol else NA_character_,
                     recorded = start))
}

name: R/read_chi_txt.R
content:
# Reader for CH Instruments text files.
# Two layouts are seen in CHI exports:
#   1. "Convert to text" export: header with date, technique, instrument and
#      parameters, CHI's own results, then a column line such as "Potential/V, Current/A"
#      or "Time/sec, Current/A", and comma-separated rows. Every technique is written this
#      way: CV and LSV, DPV, OCP, i-t, chronoamperometry, multi-potential steps,
#      chronopotentiometry, and bipotentiostat runs with a second current (i2/A).
#   2. Headerless, tab-separated, four columns: potential (V), current (A),
#      cumulative charge (C) and time (s). No parameters are stored, so the scan
#      rate is recovered from potential and time.

# CHI column labels and the names used everywhere else in the app
# (square wave: the difference current is the response, forward and reverse are kept)
chi_columns = c("Potential/V" = "E_V", "Current/A" = "I_A", "i1/A" = "I_A", "i2/A" = "I2_A",
                "Time/sec" = "t_s", "Charge/C" = "Q_C", "Diff(i/A)" = "I_A", "For(i/A)" = "I_fwd_A", "Rev(i/A)" = "I_rev_A")

# "Data only" text exports carry numbers alone. The columns CHI writes for each technique
# (checked against exports with headers, October 2026):
#   CV, LSV: potential, current, charge, time      SWV: potential, difference, forward, reverse current
#   DPV, NPV: potential, current                   i-t, CA: time, current, charge
#   OCP, CP: time, potential                       A.C. impedance: frequency, Z', Z'', |Z|, phase
# The technique is taken from the file name when it says (SWV, DPV, OCP, EIS, ...), otherwise
# from the number of columns and how they relate to each other.
chi_dataonly = function(m, name) {
  nm = toupper(name); has = function(p) grepl(paste0("(^|[^A-Z])(", p, ")([^A-Z]|$)"), nm)
  hint = if (has("EIS|IMPEDANCE|IMP")) "eis" else if (has("SWV|SWSV")) "swv" else if (has("DPV|DPSV|NPV")) "dpv" else if (has("OCP|OCPT")) "ocp" else
    if (has("CP|CHRONOPOT")) "cp" else if (has("CA|CC|I-T|IT|CHRONOAMP")) "ca" else if (has("CV|LSV")) "cv" else ""
  v = function(j) as.numeric(m[, j]); n = ncol(m)
  tech = if (n == 5) "eis" else if (n == 4) {
    if (hint == "swv" || stats::median(abs(v(2) - (v(3) - v(4)))) < 1e-3 * stats::median(abs(v(2))) + 1e-15) "swv" else "cv"
  } else if (n == 3) "ca" else if (n == 2) {
    if (hint %in% c("ocp", "cp", "dpv", "cv")) hint else if (max(abs(v(2))) > 0.01) "ocp" else "dpv"
  } else stop("Unrecognised data-only layout in ", name, ": ", n, " columns")
  how = if (nzchar(hint) && (hint == tech || (hint == "cp" && tech == "ocp"))) "file name" else "column layout"
  d = switch(tech,
    eis = data.frame(freq_Hz = v(1), Z = complex(real = v(2), imaginary = v(3))),
    swv = data.frame(E_V = v(1), I_A = v(2), I_fwd_A = v(3), I_rev_A = v(4)),
    cv  = data.frame(E_V = v(1), I_A = v(2), Q_C = v(3), t_s = v(4)),
    ca  = data.frame(t_s = v(1), I_A = v(2), Q_C = v(3)),
    dpv = data.frame(E_V = v(1), I_A = v(2)),
    ocp = , cp = data.frame(t_s = v(1), E_V = v(2)))
  label = c(eis = "A.C. Impedance", swv = "Square Wave Voltammetry", cv = "Cyclic or Linear Sweep Voltammetry", ca = "Chronoamperometry (i-t)",
            dpv = "Pulse Voltammetry (DPV or NPV)", ocp = "Open Circuit Potential", cp = "Chronopotentiometry")[[tech]]
  list(tech = tech, data = d, technique = paste0(label, " (data-only export, technique from the ", how, ")"))
}

read_chi_txt = function(path, name = basename(path)) {
  lines = sub("\r$", "", readLines(path, warn = FALSE))
  num = "^\\s*[-+]?[0-9]*\\.?[0-9]+([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?\\s*$"

  hdr_i = grep("^(Potential/V|Time/sec)", lines)[1]
  if (!is.na(hdr_i)) {
    params = parse_chi_header(lines[1:(hdr_i - 1)])
    cols = trimws(strsplit(lines[hdr_i], ",")[[1]])
    body = lines[(hdr_i + 1):length(lines)]
    body = body[nzchar(trimws(body))]
    m = do.call(rbind, strsplit(body, ","))
    data = as.data.frame(apply(m, 2, as.numeric))
    names(data) = ifelse(cols %in% names(chi_columns), chi_columns[cols], make.names(cols))
    layout = "chi_export"
  } else {
    body = lines[nzchar(trimws(lines))]
    sep = if (grepl("\t", body[1])) "\t" else ","
    first = trimws(strsplit(body[1], sep)[[1]])
    if (length(first) < 2 || !all(grepl(num, first)))
      stop("Unrecognised CHI text layout in ", name)
    m = do.call(rbind, lapply(strsplit(body, sep), trimws))
    x = chi_dataonly(m, name)
    if (x$tech == "eis")
      return(list(file = name, kind = "eis", layout = "headerless", params = list(technique = x$technique), data = x$data, note = ""))
    data = x$data
    params = list(technique = x$technique, instrument = NA_character_, scan_rate_V_s = NA_real_)
    if (x$tech == "cv") {
      dt = stats::median(diff(data$t_s)); dE = stats::median(abs(diff(data$E_V)))
      params = c(params[1:2], list(scan_rate_V_s = round(dE / dt, 6), sample_interval_V = dE, high_E_V = max(data$E_V), low_E_V = min(data$E_V)))
    }
    layout = "headerless_tab"
  }

  # Sweeps only exist when potential is the swept variable (first column). In a
  # time-based file (OCP, chronopotentiometry) the potential drifts and has no sweeps.
  data$segment = if (names(data)[1] == "E_V") assign_segments(data$E_V) else 1L
  if (names(data)[1] == "E_V" && !is.null(params$segments) && !is.na(params$segments) &&
      max(data$segment) != params$segments)
    warning(basename(path), ": found ", max(data$segment), " segments, header says ", params$segments)

  list(file = name, layout = layout, params = params, data = data,
       chi_peaks = attr(params, "peaks"))
}

# Segments are the sweeps between turning points, where the direction of the
# potential step changes sign.
assign_segments = function(E) {
  d = sign(diff(E))
  d[d == 0] = NA
  d = zoo_fill(d)
  seg = c(1, 1 + cumsum(diff(d) != 0))
  c(seg, seg[length(seg)])
}

zoo_fill = function(x) {
  for (i in seq_along(x)[-1]) if (is.na(x[i])) x[i] = x[i - 1]
  if (is.na(x[1])) x[1] = x[which(!is.na(x))[1]]
  x
}

parse_chi_header = function(h) {
  get = function(key) {
    ln = grep(paste0("^", key), h, value = TRUE)[1]
    if (is.na(ln)) return(NA_character_)
    trimws(sub("^[^=:]*[=:]", "", ln))
  }
  getn = function(key) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(get(key)))
  p = list(
    date = h[1], technique = h[2],
    instrument = get("Instrument Model"),
    init_E_V = getn("Init E \\(V\\)"), high_E_V = getn("High E \\(V\\)"),
    low_E_V = getn("Low E \\(V\\)"), scan_rate_V_s = getn("Scan Rate \\(V/s\\)"),
    segments = getn("Segment ="), sample_interval_V = getn("Sample Interval \\(V\\)"),
    quiet_time_s = getn("Quiet Time"), sensitivity_A_V = getn("Sensitivity"),
    channel = suppressWarnings(as.integer(sub("^Channel ([0-9]+):.*", "\\1",
                                              grep("^Channel [0-9]+:", h, value = TRUE)[1])))
  )
  # Every "Name = value" setting, so each technique can find its own (E1 (V), T1 (s),
  # Cycle, Pulse Width (sec), Cathodic Current (A), 2nd E (V) and so on). Numbers are
  # stored as numbers; "30." and similar CHI spellings are read too.
  kv = grep("^[^=]+=[^=]+$", h, value = TRUE)
  key = trimws(sub("=.*$", "", kv))
  val = trimws(sub("^[^=]*=", "", kv))
  nv = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(val))
  p$settings = stats::setNames(lapply(seq_along(val), function(i) if (is.na(nv[i])) val[i] else nv[i]), key)

  # CHI writes its own peak results after the channel line; keep them so the
  # pipeline's peaks can be checked against the instrument software.
  start = grep("^Channel [0-9]+:", h)[1]
  peaks = NULL
  if (!is.na(start) && start < length(h)) {
    seg = NA
    rec = list()
    cur = list()
    for (ln in h[(start + 1):length(h)]) {
      if (grepl("^Segment [0-9]+:", ln)) seg = as.integer(sub("^Segment ([0-9]+):.*", "\\1", ln))
      else if (grepl("^Ep = ", ln)) cur = list(segment = seg, Ep_V = as.numeric(sub("^Ep = ([^V]+)V.*", "\\1", ln)))
      else if (grepl("^ip = ", ln)) cur$ip_A = as.numeric(sub("^ip = ([^A]+)A.*", "\\1", ln))
      else if (grepl("^Ah = ", ln)) { cur$Ah_C = as.numeric(sub("^Ah = ([^C]+)C.*", "\\1", ln)); rec[[length(rec) + 1]] = as.data.frame(cur) }
    }
    if (length(rec)) peaks = do.call(rbind, rec)
  }
  attr(p, "peaks") = peaks
  p
}

# One setting from the header, or a default when the file does not have it
chi_setting = function(x, key, default = NA) {
  v = x$params$settings[[key]]
  if (is.null(v)) default else v
}

name: R/read_emf16_grf.R
content:
# Reader for data files written by Lawson Labs EMF16_grf.
# Layout follows section F of the EMF16_grf manual: a header row starting with
# "Time / s", one column per channel, values in volts, an optional comment typed
# during the run, then a footer of run settings. Real EMF16 files are
# tab-separated and label channels with spaces ("1 - 1"); the manual's printed
# sample is space-separated ("1-7"), so both are handled.

read_emf16_grf = function(path) {
  lines = sub("\r$", "", readLines(path, warn = FALSE))

  hdr_i = grep("^\\s*Time\\s*/\\s*s", lines)[1]
  if (is.na(hdr_i)) stop("No 'Time / s' header found. Is this an EMF16_grf file?")
  tabbed = grepl("\t", lines[hdr_i])
  split_line = function(x) if (tabbed) strsplit(x, "\t") else strsplit(trimws(x), "[\t ]+")

  # Channel labels are "n-m" (spaces allowed around the dash); anything else on
  # the header line is the comment column title, not a channel.
  hdr = split_line(sub("^\\s*Time\\s*/\\s*s\\s*", "", lines[hdr_i]))[[1]]
  hdr = gsub("\\s", "", hdr)
  channels = hdr[grepl("^[0-9]+-[0-9]+$", hdr)]
  n_ch = length(channels)
  if (n_ch == 0) stop("No channel labels found in the header")

  body = lines[(hdr_i + 1):length(lines)]
  body = body[nzchar(trimws(body))]
  is_data = grepl("^\\s*[0-9]+\\.?[0-9]*\\s", body)
  footer = trimws(body[!is_data])

  # Fill a character matrix in one step (rows = data lines, columns = fields);
  # per-row loops made a 17,000-row file take several seconds.
  tok = split_line(body[is_data])
  lens = lengths(tok)
  m = matrix("", nrow = length(tok), ncol = max(lens, n_ch + 1))
  m[cbind(rep(seq_along(tok), lens), sequence(lens))] = trimws(unlist(tok, use.names = FALSE))
  wide = data.frame(time_s = as.numeric(m[, 1]))
  for (j in seq_len(n_ch)) wide[[channels[j]]] = as.numeric(m[, j + 1])
  # A comment typed during the run sits after the channel values on that row
  if (ncol(m) > n_ch + 1) {
    extra = trimws(gsub("\\s+", " ", do.call(paste, as.data.frame(m[, -(1:(n_ch + 1)), drop = FALSE]))))
    wide$comment = ifelse(nzchar(extra), extra, NA_character_)
  } else {
    wide$comment = NA_character_
  }

  # Long format is what the plateau and calibration steps use; mV because ISE
  # slopes are reported in mV per decade.
  long = data.frame(
    time_s = rep(wide$time_s, n_ch),
    channel = rep(channels, each = nrow(wide)),
    emf_mV = unlist(wide[channels], use.names = FALSE) * 1000
  )

  kv = regmatches(footer, regexec("^([^:]+):\\s*(.*)$", footer))
  kv = kv[lengths(kv) == 3]
  settings = setNames(trimws(vapply(kv, `[`, "", 3)), trimws(vapply(kv, `[`, "", 2)))

  # The logging interval comes from the footer; time is printed to 0.1 s, so at
  # fast intervals consecutive rows share a time stamp. Logging switched off and
  # on leaves a jump in time, flagged so later steps do not average across it.
  interval = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(settings["Applied Interval"]))
  if (is.na(interval)) interval = stats::median(diff(wide$time_s)[diff(wide$time_s) > 0])
  dt = diff(wide$time_s)
  gaps = which(dt > max(3 * interval, 0.3))

  if (any(abs(long$emf_mV) > 5000, na.rm = TRUE))
    warning("Values above 5 V after conversion. The file may already be in mV.")

  list(
    file = basename(path), channels = channels, wide = wide, long = long,
    comments = wide[!is.na(wide$comment), c("time_s", "comment")],
    settings = settings, interval_s = interval,
    gaps = data.frame(after_s = wide$time_s[gaps], resumes_s = wide$time_s[gaps + 1])
  )
}

R/read_pine_txt.R
content:
# Reader for Pine Research AfterMath text exports (WaveDriver bipotentiostats).
# The export puts every trace side by side, four columns each (Index, Segment, x, y),
# under a "Trace Name:" row and a units row. Each trace appears twice, once as a trace
# and once as a result, and the two copies can use different units (mA in one, µA in
# the other), and so can different files of the same experiment. Units are therefore
# always read from the header, never assumed.
# K1 is the first working electrode (the disk of an RRDE), K2 the second (the ring).
# The measured traces ("vs Time") are used; "Applied Potential" is the programmed
# waveform at a much finer time step and is not a measurement.

pine_units = c("V" = 1, "mV" = 1e-3, "uV" = 1e-6,
               "A" = 1, "mA" = 1e-3, "uA" = 1e-6, "nA" = 1e-9, "pA" = 1e-12,
               "s" = 1, "ms" = 1e-3)

read_pine_txt = function(path) {
  lines = readLines(path, warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
  lines = sub("\r$", "", lines)
  lines[1] = sub("^[^P]*Plot", "Plot", lines[1])          # drops a byte-order mark
  if (!grepl("^Plot Name:", lines[1])) stop(basename(path), " is not an AfterMath text export")
  split = function(x) strsplit(x, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  name_row = split(lines[grep("^Trace Name:", lines)[1]])
  unit_row = split(lines[grep("^Index,", lines)[1]])
  starts = which(name_row %in% c("Trace Name:", "Result Name:"))
  first = starts[!duplicated(name_row[starts + 1])]       # first copy of each trace
  # all rows into one character matrix, padded to the widest row, so each column is read once
  rows = strsplit(lines[(grep("^Index,", lines)[1] + 1):length(lines)], ",", fixed = TRUE)
  width = max(lengths(rows))
  body = do.call(rbind, lapply(rows, function(r) c(r, rep("", width - length(r)))))

  # the unit is the text in brackets; the micro sign can arrive as U+00B5, U+03BC or a
  # mis-decoded pair, so anything before the letters is read as "u"
  unit = function(h) {
    u = sub("[)].*$", "", sub("^.*[(]", "", h))
    u = sub("^[^A-Za-z]+", "u", u)
    if (u %in% names(pine_units)) pine_units[[u]] else stop("Unknown unit '", h, "' in ", basename(path))
  }
  block = function(i) {
    num = function(k) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(body[, k]))
    x = num(i + 2); y = num(i + 3)
    ok = !is.na(x) & !is.na(y)
    data.frame(segment = num(i + 1)[ok], x = x[ok] * unit(unit_row[i + 2]), y = y[ok] * unit(unit_row[i + 3]))
  }
  traces = stats::setNames(lapply(first, block), name_row[first + 1])
  pick = function(name) traces[[name]]
  k1i = pick("K1 Current vs Time"); k1e = pick("K1 Potential vs Time")
  if (is.null(k1i) || is.null(k1e)) stop(basename(path), ": no K1 current and potential traces found")
  data = data.frame(t_s = k1i$x, E_V = k1e$y[seq_len(nrow(k1i))], I_A = k1i$y)
  k2i = pick("K2 Current vs Time"); k2e = pick("K2 Potential vs Time")
  if (!is.null(k2i) && nrow(k2i) == nrow(data)) { data$I2_A = k2i$y; data$E2_V = k2e$y }
  data$segment = assign_segments(data$E_V)
  dt = stats::median(diff(data$t_s)); dE = stats::median(abs(diff(data$E_V)))
  params = list(technique = "Pine AfterMath export", instrument = "Pine WaveDriver",
                scan_rate_V_s = round(dE / dt, 4), high_E_V = max(data$E_V), low_E_V = min(data$E_V),
                ring_E_V = if (!is.null(data$E2_V)) stats::median(data$E2_V) else NA)
  list(file = basename(path), layout = "pine_aftermath", params = params, data = data,
       traces = names(traces))
}

# One reader for any supported file: CHI text, Pine AfterMath text
read_echem = function(path, name = basename(path), instrument = "auto") {
  fmt = instrument_format(path, name, instrument)
  if (fmt == "pssession") {
    x = read_pssession(path, name)
    if (x$kind == "eis") stop(name, " is an impedance measurement: open it in the Impedance (EIS) tab")
    return(x)
  }
  x = switch(fmt, biologic = read_biologic_mpt(path, name), mpr = read_biologic_mpr(path, name), gamry = read_gamry_dta(path, name),
             pine = read_pine_txt(path), chi = read_chi_txt(path, name), abf = read_abf(path, name), text = read_generic_text(path, name))
  if (is.null(x) || identical(x$kind, "eis")) stop(name, " is an impedance measurement: open it in the Impedance (EIS) tab")
  x$file = name
  x
}

name: R/read_pssession.R
content:
# Reader for PalmSens PSTrace session files (.pssession). A session is a JSON document
# stored as UTF-16 text (checked on PSTrace 5.11 files, October 2026). Each measurement
# holds a DataSet of arrays; each array names its quantity and its unit, and the unit
# type carries the scale (for example PalmSens.Units.MicroAmpere), so currents are
# converted to A from the unit given in the file, never assumed.
# Voltammetry and amperometry come back in the same form as read_chi_txt() (data with
# E_V, I_A, t_s, Q_C and a scan column; params with the scan rate and the method
# settings), so every technique tab can use them. Impedance comes back as freq_Hz and Z
# (complex, imaginary part as measured: the file stores -Z'').

pssession_scale = function(type) {
  s = c(PicoAmpere = 1e-12, NanoAmpere = 1e-9, MicroAmpere = 1e-6, MilliAmpere = 1e-3, Ampere = 1,
        NanoCoulomb = 1e-9, MicroCoulomb = 1e-6, MilliCoulomb = 1e-3, Coulomb = 1,
        MicroVolt = 1e-6, MilliVolt = 1e-3, Volt = 1, Time = 1, Hertz = 1, ZRe = 1, ZIm = 1, Z = 1, Phase = 1)
  k = sub("^PalmSens[.]Units[.]", "", type)
  if (k %in% names(s)) s[[k]] else NA_real_   # unknown scale: the array is kept out, see get() below
}

read_pssession_json = function(path) {
  b = readBin(path, "raw", file.info(path)$size)
  txt = if (length(b) >= 2 && b[1] == as.raw(0xFF) && b[2] == as.raw(0xFE)) iconv(list(b), "UTF-16LE", "UTF-8") else rawToChar(b)
  txt = gsub("﻿", "", txt, fixed = TRUE)
  txt = substr(txt, 1, max(gregexpr("}", txt, fixed = TRUE)[[1]]))   # PSTrace adds a mark after the JSON object
  jsonlite::fromJSON(txt, simplifyVector = FALSE)
}

method_settings = function(m) {
  l = strsplit(m, "\r?\n")[[1]]; l = l[grepl("^[A-Z_0-9]+=", l)]
  stats::setNames(as.list(sub("^[^=]+=", "", l)), sub("=.*$", "", l))
}

read_pssession = function(path, name = basename(path), measurement = 1) {
  j = read_pssession_json(path)
  if (!identical(j$Type, "PalmSens.DataFiles.SessionFile")) stop(name, " is not a PalmSens session file")
  me = j$Measurements[[measurement]]
  st = method_settings(me$Method %||% j$MethodForMeasurement)
  arr = lapply(me$DataSet$Values, function(v) list(desc = v$Description %||% "", q = v$Unit$Q %||% "", type = v$Unit$Type %||% "",
    values = vapply(v$DataValues, function(d) if (is.null(d$V)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(d$V), 0) * pssession_scale(v$Unit$Type %||% "")))
  qs = vapply(arr, `[[`, "", "q")
  # an array is used only when its unit scale is known; an unknown scale stops the read
  # rather than returning values that could be off by a factor of a thousand
  get = function(q, d = NULL) {
    k = which(qs == q & (is.null(d) | vapply(arr, `[[`, "", "desc") %in% d)); if (!length(k)) return(NULL)
    v = arr[[k[1]]]; if (anyNA(v$values) && all(is.na(v$values))) stop(name, ": unknown unit '", v$type, "' for ", q)
    v$values }
  params = list(file = name, technique = st$METHOD_ID %||% me$Title, title = me$Title, settings = st,
                scan_rate_V_s = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(st$SCAN_RATE %||% NA)), date = me$TimeStamp)
  if (identical(st$METHOD_ID, "eis") || any(qs == "Z'")) {
    zi = get("-Z''"); zi = if (!is.null(zi)) -zi else get("Z''")
    d = data.frame(freq_Hz = get("Frequency"), Z = complex(real = get("Z'"), imaginary = zi))
    d = d[is.finite(d$freq_Hz) & d$freq_Hz > 0, ]
    return(list(file = name, kind = "eis", params = params, data = d[order(-d$freq_Hz), ], note = ""))
  }
  # voltammetry and amperometry: one block of arrays per scan, in the order stored
  desc = vapply(arr, `[[`, "", "desc")
  # a scan is a description shared by a potential and a current array; chronopotentiometry and
  # other single-curve runs label each array by its own quantity ("potential", "current"), so they form one block
  scans = Filter(function(s) all(c("Potential", "Current") %in% qs[desc == s]), unique(desc[qs %in% c("Potential", "Current")]))
  if (!length(scans)) scans = list(NULL)
  t_all = get("Time")
  blocks = lapply(seq_along(scans), function(i) {
    s = scans[[i]]; E = get("Potential", s); I = get("Current", s); Q = get("Charge", s)
    n = max(length(E), length(I))
    t = if (length(t_all) == n) t_all else rep(NA_real_, n)
    data.frame(scan = i, E_V = if (length(E)) E else NA, I_A = I, t_s = t, Q_C = if (length(Q) == n) Q else NA)
  })
  d = do.call(rbind, blocks)
  # sweep segments (a new one at every change of direction), as in the CHI reader, for the CV analyses
  dir = sign(diff(d$E_V)); dir[dir == 0] = NA; dir = c(dir[1], dir)
  for (i in seq_along(dir)[-1]) if (is.na(dir[i])) dir[i] = dir[i - 1]
  d$segment = cumsum(c(1, diff(dir) != 0))
  # time runs from zero in every scan; make it continuous so the whole run can be plotted against time
  if (length(blocks) > 1 && !anyNA(d$t_s)) { per = vapply(blocks, function(b) max(b$t_s, na.rm = TRUE), 0); d$t_s = d$t_s + c(0, cumsum(per))[d$scan] }
  list(file = name, kind = "voltammetry", params = params, data = d)
}

# A session file is recognised by its UTF-16 mark and the PalmSens type
is_pssession = function(path) {
  b = readBin(path, "raw", 200)
  length(b) >= 2 && b[1] == as.raw(0xFF) && b[2] == as.raw(0xFE) &&
    grepl("PalmSens", iconv(list(b[3:length(b)]), "UTF-16LE", "UTF-8", sub = ""), fixed = TRUE)
}
